"They're opening up the North Sea oil," Trump told reporters at the White House before departing for a campaign trip to Florida ahead of the November 3 midterm US elections. "I've been after them to do that for two years... Andy is getting it done." On Wednesday, Trump praised Britain's North Sea oil exploration after the UK ended years of legal and political wrangling to approved the [USN:L8N46707X TEXT:"Jackdaw North Sea gas field"], though British officials said a decision about the bigger Rosebank oilfield was yet to be made.

item.title: PwC confirms cybersecurity incident involving employee learning records
item.description: PwC on Friday said it was aware of a cybersecurity incident involving a third-party vendor used to host company employee learning records, the day after a cyber extortion group claimed to have stolen 590 gigabytes of company data.
item.dc:creator: A.J. Vicens
item.content:encoded: PwC on Friday said it was aware of a cybersecurity incident involving a third-party vendor used to host company employee learning records, the day after a cyber extortion group claimed to have stolen 590 gigabytes of company data. A PwC global spokesperson said "the affected site does not house client data, sensitive personal data or financial information. Once we learned of this incident we acted promptly to secure the environment and conduct a thorough review." The incident "does not impact our network or any of our operations," the spokesperson said. A cyber extortion group called "Everest" claimed responsibility for the data breach in a message posted to its website October 22, according to cybercrime research platform eCrime.ch. The message included a countdown timer with five days remaining, and a message indicating the data would be released if a deal could not be reached. Everest claimed to have stolen 590 gigabytes of data that included "regional HR and learning exports, integration documentation, software components and PwC e-learning courses." The data contains information "about individuals and their organisational and employment history," Everest said, including names, email addresses, telephone numbers, addresses and other details. The PwC spokesperson declined to comment on the amount of data stolen or the veracity of the hacking group's claims.

item.title: Rendimientos EEUU suben ligeramente, título a 10 años sigue por debajo 5% ante nerviosismo por IA
item.description: Los rendimientos de los bonos del Tesoro de Estados Unidos subían el viernes, un día después de que el rendimiento de referencia a 10 años registrara su mayor caída diaria en casi cuatro años, aunque se mantenían bajo el umbral del 5% debido a la persistente preocupación por la sostenibilidad del repunte de las acciones relacionadas con la IA.
item.dc:creator: Chuck Mikolajczak
item.content:encoded: Los rendimientos de los bonos del Tesoro de Estados Unidos subían el viernes, un día después de que el rendimiento de referencia a 10 años registrara su mayor caída diaria en casi cuatro años, aunque se mantenían bajo el umbral del 5% debido a la persistente preocupación por la sostenibilidad del repunte de las acciones relacionadas con la IA. * El rendimiento a 10 años se desplomó 19,3 puntos básicos el jueves, su mayor caída desde el 10 de marzo de 2023, cuando las autoridades reguladoras cerraron SVB Financial Group tras el intento fallido del banco de obtener capital. * Las recientes preocupaciones sobre la sostenibilidad del "repunte de la IA", un componente clave del actual mercado alcista de la renta variable, han empujado a los inversionistas hacia activos más seguros, como la deuda pública, a pesar de que los datos económicos apuntan a que persisten las presiones sobre los precios y de que los precios del petróleo han superado la barrera de los 100 dólares por barril. * Las acciones estadounidenses cotizaban a la baja en las primeras horas de negociación, aunque el sector tecnológico del S&P 500 (.SPLRCT) registraba una subida en la jornada. * El rendimiento del bono del Tesoro estadounidense a 10 años de referencia subía 3,7 puntos básicos, hasta el 4,992%. El rendimiento a 10 años ha bajado unos 11 puntos en la semana y va camino de registrar su tercera semana consecutiva de descensos, su racha bajista más larga desde junio. * Los rendimientos ampliaron sus ganancias después de que S&P Global anunciara que su índice preliminar PMI compuesto de producción de Estados Unidos, que mide los sectores manufacturero y de servicios, bajó este mes a 57,6 desde el máximo de cinco años registrado en septiembre (58,4), aunque se mantuvo muy por encima del umbral de 50 que indica expansión. * El rendimiento del bono a 30 años ganaba 2,8 puntos básicos hasta el 5,315% y registraba un descenso de casi 13 puntos básicos en la semana, encaminándose además hacia su tercera semana consecutiva de caídas. * A pesar de que los datos económicos apuntan a un aumento de las presiones sobre los precios, las expectativas del mercado respecto a una subida de tasas por parte de la Fed en su reunión de política monetaria de la próxima semana se han desvanecido. La probabilidad de una subida de al menos 25 puntos básicos se ha reducido al 8,3%, según el CME FedWatch, desde el 15,5% de hace una semana y el 70,9% de hace un mes. * Un indicador muy seguido de la curva de rendimientos de los bonos del Tesoro de EEUU, que mide la diferencia entre los rendimientos de los bonos a 2 y a 10 años —y que se considera un indicador de las expectativas económicas—, se situó en 30,8 puntos básicos positivos. * Otros datos de las encuestas a consumidores de la Universidad de Míchigan mostraron que su índice de confianza del consumidor cayó este mes hasta 48,0 desde una lectura final de 48,1 en septiembre. * El rendimiento de los bonos del Tesoro de Estados Unidos a 2 años , que suele evolucionar en consonancia con las expectativas sobre las tasas de interés de la Fed, subía 4,5 puntos básicos hasta el 4,68%, aunque registraba un descenso de unos 5 puntos básicos en la semana. El rendimiento a 2 años se encaminaba hacia su cuarta semana consecutiva de descensos, su racha más larga del año.

item.title: Trump afirma que Canadá "está trabajando muy duro" para llegar a un acuerdo con EEUU
item.description: El presidente de Estados Unidos, Donald Trump, afirmó el viernes que Canadá está trabajando duro para alcanzar un acuerdo comercial.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: El presidente de Estados Unidos, Donald Trump, afirmó el viernes que Canadá está trabajando duro para alcanzar un acuerdo comercial. "Canadá está trabajando muy duro para llegar a un acuerdo con nosotros, y aunque me duele decirlo, tenemos todas las cartas en la mano", declaró Trump a la prensa en la Casa Blanca. El Gobierno canadiense no respondió de inmediato a una solicitud de comentarios. Estados Unidos y Canadá se encuentran en un punto muerto comercial desde que las negociaciones se rompieron en agosto, lo que desencadenó nuevos aranceles y medidas de represalia a ambos lados de la frontera. Este colapso ha agravado la brecha entre estos aliados históricos, que se han culpado mutuamente del fracaso de las negociaciones. Esta situación ha llevado al primer ministro canadiense, Mark Carney, a instar a un mayor alejamiento del principal socio comercial de Canadá y ha sembrado dudas sobre la viabilidad del Acuerdo entre Estados Unidos, México y Canadá.

item.title: Zelenskiy says Ukrainian, Russian and US negotiators to meet in early November in Abu Dhabi
item.description: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskiy said on Friday that peace negotiators from Ukraine, Russia and the United States had agreed to meet at a technical level in the first half of November in Abu Dhabi, adding that he hoped a meeting of the countries' leaders would follow.
item.dc:creator: Andrea Shalal, Olena Harmash
item.content:encoded: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskiy said on Friday that peace negotiators from Ukraine, Russia and the United States had agreed to meet at a technical level in the first half of November in Abu Dhabi, adding that he hoped a meeting of the countries' leaders would follow. Zelenskiy said he spoke with US envoys Jared Kushner and Steve Witkoff on Friday after their meeting with Russian President Vladimir Putin earlier this week. He said any peace agreement would need strong security guarantees for Ukraine and funding for 10 years to maintain the Ukrainian army. "The plan is to meet in the first half of November, and as early as possible, of course," Zelenskiy told the Hudson Institute think tank via a video link. He said much would depend on Russia, noting that a similar meeting expected this month had not materialized. Zelenskiy stressed the importance of continued diplomatic efforts to reach a ceasefire and end the war, now in its fifth year, adding that Europe should also be involved in the talks. The Ukrainian president said it was critical for the technical discussions to be followed by a meeting of the countries' leaders. Ukraine's military was still grappling with access to Starlink communications systems, Zelenskiy said, despite US assurances that speed restrictions had been removed. "The speed limits on Starlink and Starshield are still there, and the speed has not been restored," he said, contradicting a statement by US President Donald Trump that the services had been fully restored. Ukraine was also waiting for a shipment of air defense interceptors that had been previously agreed, Zelenskiy said, complicating Ukrainian defensive efforts in the face of nearly daily massive attacks by Russian drones and missiles.

item.title: AT&T, T-Mobile tighten AI guardrails as autonomous networks remain years away
item.description: Telecom giants AT&T and T-Mobile are investing to safeguard customer data and network infrastructure from new cybersecurity threats as AI integration ramps up, though fully autonomous networks remain years away, company executives told Reuters.
item.dc:creator: Mehnaz Yasmin, Harshita Varghese
item.content:encoded: Telecom giants AT&T (T.N) and T-Mobile (TMUS.O) are investing to safeguard customer data and network infrastructure from new cybersecurity threats as AI integration ramps up, though fully autonomous networks remain years away, company executives told Reuters. As AI agents automate workflows and data analysis, with declining human intervention, cybersecurity concerns are growing across industries over access to sensitive information and connected software. For telecom operators, which manage vast amounts of customer data and critical communications infrastructure, vulnerabilities in AI systems or third-party software could extend from data breaches to network disruptions. "Yes, we are increasing our investments in how we monitor and react," T-Mobile's Chief Technology Officer John Saw told the Reuters Global Markets Forum . The company simultaneously works with vendors to ensure security holes are closed as soon as possible, he added. The Bellevue, Washington-based wireless carrier has suffered several data breaches, including incidents in 2021 and 2023, cumulatively impacting over 100 million customer accounts. It has [USN:L1N2Z32FU TEXT:"agreed"] to various [USN:L1N3LC0S9 TEXT:"settlements"] with consumers and the Federal Communications Commission involving cybersecurity penalties and investments. AT&T, meanwhile, warned that third-party software providers and AI agents pose cybersecurity risks that extend beyond operators' own networks. "There (are) industry problems, not things that AT&T can solve by itself," CTO Jeremy Legg said, questioning if the open-source community followed comparable security standards. The Texas-based company has deployed AI governance controls such as encryption, multi-factor authentication and human oversight of data access. It is also working to verify whether third-party AI agents seeking access to customer accounts are acting on behalf of legitimate customers, the company said. AI has automated aspects of network management for telecom operators, but handing over entire networks to AI-driven autonomous systems is still "years away," Legg said, as human intervention is still required to solve complex network problems. For instance, AT&T has automated some tasks such as analyzing trouble tickets to identify potential fixes and, in some cases, automatically implementing repairs. T-Mobile, meanwhile, uses AI to automatically adjust cell-site antennas when nearby sites go down to compensate for coverage gaps. During Winter Storm Fern in January, T-Mobile's self-organizing network, or SON, restored coverage to about 66% of customers within an hour and 90% within eight hours, with most customers regaining service before power was restored, Saw said. item.content:encoded: What we're watching: At 80, leftist President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva is running in a close election for an unprecedented, non-consecutive fourth term. His biggest competition is Senator Flavio Bolsonaro, the son of former far-right President Jair Bolsonaro, who narrowly lost to Lula in 2022 and was convicted for plotting a coup to overturn the result. Lula has accused the Trump administration of using tariffs and other means to interfere with Brazilian affairs. Bolsonaro has portrayed Trump as an ally, and is expected to strengthen ties with Washington if elected.

item.title: Governo deve manter subsídios a combustíveis em 2027 se cotação do petróleo seguir alta, diz Durigan
item.description: O governo do presidente Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva deverá manter subsídios a combustíveis se a cotação internacional do petróleo continuar alta por conta do conflito no Oriente Médio, disse nesta sexta-feira o ministro da Fazenda, Dario Durigan.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: O governo do presidente Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva deverá manter subsídios a combustíveis se a cotação internacional do petróleo continuar alta por conta do conflito no Oriente Médio, disse nesta sexta-feira o ministro da Fazenda, Dario Durigan. Em entrevista ao portal Uol, Durigan argumentou que o governo observa ganhos de arrecadação quando o valor do barril do petróleo sobe, tendo optado por reverter esses ganhos -- com royalties e tributos pagos por empresas do setor -- para suavizar variações de preços dos combustíveis. "Se o Brent continuar num patamar muito elevado (no próximo ano) e a gente seguir percebendo que vai ter recurso adicional, é sim possível, e acho que essa deve ser a proposta do presidente, manter essa ajuda para suavizar, não é para controlar preço", disse. O ministro acrescentou que não pode ser descartada a possibilidade de manutenção do imposto sobre exportação de petróleo nesse cenário, ressaltando que o tributo criado após a eclosão da guerra no Oriente Médio tem caráter regulatório ao desincentivar a saída de óleo do país, com efeito fiscal secundário. A cotação do petróleo Brent operava ao redor de US$117 no início da tarde desta sexta-feira. Durigan ainda afirmou que o preço dos combustíveis no Brasil explodiria se eventualmente o senador Flávio Bolsonaro (PL) fosse eleito e reinstituísse o sistema de paridade de preços de importação, modelo usado pela Petrobras até 2023 que usava cotações internacionais para balizar os reajustes de combustíveis no país. PEQUENOS NEGÓCIOS Na entrevista, o ministro acrescentou que o governo poderá apresentar propostas para liberação de crédito ou perdão de dívidas para pequenos negócios afetados pelo fim da escala 6x1, aprovado neste mês pelo Congresso Nacional. Durigan, que coordena o plano econômico para a tentativa de reeleição de Lula, ponderou que a iniciativa faz parte do escopo da campanha do petista, não do governo. Os brasileiros irão às urnas no domingo para definir, em segundo turno, se a presidência da República será ocupada por Lula em seu quarto mandato não consecutivo ou por Flávio Bolsonaro.

item.title: Turkey says renewed attack on Iran would expand conflict, diplomacy only way
item.description: Turkish Foreign Minister Hakan Fidan cautioned on Friday against any renewed attack on Iran, saying such a move would exacerbate tensions and further expand the conflict there, adding that diplomacy and dialogue were the only way to end the war.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Turkish Foreign Minister Hakan Fidan cautioned on Friday against any renewed attack on Iran, saying such a move would exacerbate tensions and further expand the conflict there, adding that diplomacy and dialogue were the only way to end the war. Fidan met his counterparts from Egypt, Pakistan, Saudi Arabia, Germany, France, Britain and Italy in Istanbul to discuss developments in the Iran war , attacks on Saudi Arabia by Iran-backed Houthi militants, and Russia's war in Ukraine . It was the [USN:L8N4680AN TEXT:"first collective meeting"] between the countries, comprising the Regional Four (R4) and EU 3 (E3), alongside Italy. "We are all in agreement that a new attack on Iran would expand the war in the region," Fidan told a press conference after the meeting. "A military intervention on Iran is not in any way a solution. Nobody approves this at the moment," he added. French Foreign Minister Jean-Noel Barrot said after Friday's meetings that renewed escalation between Iran and the United States would [USN:S8N45100D TEXT:"only have losers"] and raise oil prices. The comments followed a New York Times report on Wednesday that the US and Israeli militaries had drawn up specific plans for renewed strikes against Iran after the US midterm congressional election next month. Citing US officials, it said likely targets would include Iran's energy infrastructure, nuclear facilities, and its missile and drone arsenal. US President Donald Trump said earlier this month that the US [USN:L1N45U0PH TEXT:"would not launch an attack"] on Iran before the midterms, as Washington and Tehran were having "productive" talks about ending their six-month-old war. On Friday, [USN:S0N45103G TEXT:"he said"] the US could end the war quickly but questioned whether Washington should seek a swift conclusion or allow the conflict to gradually wind down. NATO member Turkey has been in close contact with Washington, Tehran and regional mediators to seek an end to the war. It has repeatedly called for attacks to stop and warned against the regional expansion of the conflict. Fidan also said the countries meeting on Friday had discussed possible parameters to ensure the war in Iran does not expand further, but did not elaborate. Following Friday's meetings, German Foreign Minister Johann Wadephul said Germany, France, and Britain were [USN:S8N43200V TEXT:"ready to negotiate"] with Iran to rule out its acquisition of nuclear weapons, while calling for support for Saudi Arabia and Yemen.

item.title: Senegal bank creditor committee picks Houlihan Lokey as adviser, sources say
item.description: Senegal's bank creditor committee has chosen Houlihan Lokey as its financial adviser, four people told Reuters, as the West African nation pushes ahead with plans to rework its debt.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Senegal's bank creditor committee has chosen Houlihan Lokey as its financial adviser, four people told Reuters, as the West African nation pushes ahead with [USN:L6N44T0WZ TEXT:"plans to rework its debt"]. Senegal last month announced plans to restore debt sustainability using an "enhanced" G20 Common Framework, which it hopes will speed up the process. Separate creditor committees for commercial banks and regional development institutions — alongside the standard groups representing bilateral lenders and bondholders — are part of that process, according to a presentation to creditors seen by Reuters. The government said in the presentation that it had met with bank creditors on September 25, and lenders subsequently formed a committee. Houlihan Lokey declined to comment. The firm also advises bondholder groups in Lebanon and Venezuela. Senegal's government did not immediately respond to a request for comment.

item.title: KLM cancels dozens of flights due to strong winds, spokesperson says
item.description: Airline KLM, the Dutch arm of Air France KLM , cancelled 20 flights on Friday due to strong winds in the Netherlands caused by Storm Austen, with a further 22 cancellations expected on Saturday, a spokesperson said.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Airline KLM, the Dutch arm of Air France KLM (AIRF.PA) , cancelled 20 flights on Friday due to strong winds in the Netherlands caused by [USN:L1N4690I7 TEXT:"Storm Austen"], with a further 22 cancellations expected on Saturday, a spokesperson said. The Dutch weather service (KNMI) warned that heavy wind gusts of 75 to 90 km per hour were expected in several parts of the country on Friday and throughout the weekend Schiphol airport, one of Europe's busiest hubs, told Dutch news agency ANP that it was experiencing little disruption from the weather conditions, with no other airlines cancelling flights for the same reason Storm Austen disrupted power supplies and transport across several European countries on Friday, leaving nearly 300,000 French homes and 12,000 British homes without electricity amid strong winds and heavy rain

item.title: Bayern coach Kompany taken to hospital after collapsing during training session
item.description: Bayern Munich coach Vincent Kompany was rushed to hospital on Friday after collapsing during a training session, the German champions said.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Bayern Munich coach Vincent Kompany was rushed to hospital on Friday after collapsing during a training session, the German champions said. The Belgian had been [USN:L6N46610X TEXT:"nursing"] a virus in recent days and had missed some of his team's training sessions. "On Friday, Vincent Kompany required medical attention after collapsing during a training session for Bayern’s reserve team," the club said. "The head coach of the professional squad had been observing the second team’s session." "Kompany is currently undergoing a thorough examination in the hospital and will remain under medical care. For the time being, his coaching staff will manage all training and match-related operations." The Bundesliga leaders, who drew 2-2 at home against Arsenal in the Champions League earlier this week, are due to travel to Freiburg on Sunday. “Vincent Kompany’s health is our top priority," said Max Eberl, Bayern's Board Member for Sport. "At Bayern, we will do everything we can to ensure he makes a speedy recovery." "Vinnie is receiving all the necessary medical care and support, and he will be given as much time as he needs. Everyone at FC Bayern wishes Vinnie a quick recovery.”

item.title: Zelenski dice que negociadores de Ucrania, Rusia y EEUU se reunirán en noviembre en Abu Dabi
item.description: El presidente de Ucrania, Volodímir Zelenski, dijo el viernes que los negociadores de paz de su país se reunirán a nivel técnico con los de Rusia y Estados Unidos durante la primera quincena de noviembre en Abu Dabi, y añadió que espera que luego haya una cita entre los líderes de los países.
item.dc:creator: Andrea Shalal, Olena Harmash
item.content:encoded: El presidente de Ucrania, Volodímir Zelenski, dijo el viernes que los negociadores de paz de su país se reunirán a nivel técnico con los de Rusia y Estados Unidos durante la primera quincena de noviembre en Abu Dabi, y añadió que espera que luego haya una cita entre los líderes de los países. Zelenski dijo que habló el viernes con los enviados estadounidenses Jared Kushner y Steve Witkoff tras la reunión que estos mantuvieron con el presidente ruso, Vladimir Putin, a principios de esta semana. Asimismo, indicó que cualquier acuerdo de paz necesitará sólidas garantías de seguridad para Ucrania y financiación durante diez años para mantener el ejército ucraniano. "El plan es reunirnos en la primera quincena de noviembre y, por supuesto, lo antes posible", dijo Zelenski al centro de estudios Hudson Institute por videoconferencia. Agregó que mucho dependería de Rusia y destacó que una reunión similar prevista para este mes no se había materializado. Zelenski subrayó la importancia de proseguir con los esfuerzos diplomáticos para alcanzar un alto el fuego y poner fin a la guerra, que ya cumple su quinto año, y añadió que Europa también debería participar en las negociaciones. El presidente ucraniano señaló que es fundamental que las conversaciones técnicas vayan seguidas de una reunión de los líderes de los países. Las fuerzas armadas ucranianas siguen teniendo dificultades para acceder a los sistemas de comunicaciones Starlink, señaló Zelenski, a pesar de las garantías de Washington de que se habían eliminado las restricciones de velocidad. "Los límites de velocidad en Starlink y Starshield siguen vigentes, y la velocidad no se ha restablecido", afirmó, contradiciendo una declaración de su par estadounidense, Donald Trump, según la cual los servicios se habían restablecido por completo. Ucrania también estaba a la espera de un envío de interceptores de defensa aérea que se había acordado previamente, señaló Zelenski, lo que complica los esfuerzos defensivos de su país ante los ataques masivos, casi diarios, de drones y misiles rusos.

item.title: Trump says Canada 'working very hard' to make a deal with US
item.description: US President Donald Trump on Friday that Canada is working hard to make a trade deal with the US.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: US President Donald Trump on Friday that Canada is working hard to make a trade deal with the US. "Canada is working very hard to make a deal with us, and I hate to say this, but we have all the cards," Trump told reporters at the White House. The Canadian government did not immediately respond to a request for comment. The US and Canada have been locked in a trade standoff since talks broke down in August, triggering new tariffs and retaliation on both sides of the border. The breakdown has widened a rift between the longtime allies, who have blamed each other for the failed talks, spurred Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney to urge a further shift away from Canada's biggest trading partner, and cast doubt on the viability of the US-Mexico-Canada Agreement.

item.title: Some Parisians buy pepper spray and tear gas, citing self-defence ahead of protests
item.description: Parisians are buying tear-gas cannisters and pepper sprays to defend themselves and their property during protests, which are expected to continue over the weekend, the owner of a weapons shop in the French capital told Reuters.
item.dc:creator: Elizabeth Howcroft, Ardee Napolitano
item.content:encoded: Parisians are buying tear-gas cannisters and pepper sprays to defend themselves and their property during protests, which are expected to continue over the weekend, the owner of a weapons shop in the French capital told Reuters. France was hit by its worst social unrest in years last weekend as [USN:L1N4680WV TEXT:"nationwide protests"] over high prices and declining public services erupted into riots. A town hall was torched, shops pillaged and buildings covered in graffiti as violent groups clashed with police in cities across the country. Police have authorised only a union demonstration in Paris on Saturday, [USN:L1N4690GR TEXT:"rejecting requests"] for rallies lodged by France's main student union, UNEF, and the anti-establishment Yellow Vest movement. At the Armurerie de la Bourse weapons shop in central Paris, owner Yves Gollety told Reuters he has seen a big increase in the sale of non-lethal weapons since the weekend. Shops just 30 metres (33 yards) away had been looted, with their shutters torn off, he said. "It's the first time that we've seen such an increase, and with all segments of the population," Gollety said, adding that his customers include shopkeepers, restaurant owners and individuals. "People have been physically traumatised and are afraid," he said. The top-selling products are pepper sprays and tear-gas cannisters, which Gollety said could only be used in self-defence. Gollety, who is also president of the national association of gunsmiths, told French newspaper Le Parisien that orders had increased tenfold. Members of the public are only allowed to buy small cannisters under 100 millilitres in size, Gollety said. Reuters found no evidence that people in Paris were buying other types of weapons in response to the protests. Alain Di Crescenzo, the president of France's chamber of commerce, urged shopkeepers to refrain from using weapons to defend their businesses. Speaking on the radio station Europe 1 on Friday, he said that he had personally seen shopkeepers arming themselves with baseball bats, crowbars and shotguns. Reuters was not able to independently verify this. “It’s extremely worrying,” he said. “It’s not their job to do that... It would add suffering onto suffering." "The police must be left to do their jobs and I recommend the utmost caution," he added. "YOU HAVE TO BE PREPARED" A shopkeeper who sells motorbikes and scooters in Paris' 15th arrondissement told Reuters he bought three large tear-gas cannisters, plus another small one, to protect his shop. "You can be taken by surprise, with people arriving without any prior warning. So you have to be prepared," said the shopkeeper, who asked not to be identified. France's government has pledged [USN:L1N4670D4 TEXT:"tougher security"], and will deploy 70,000 police backed by specialist units for protests on Saturday, but the increase in people considering how to defend themselves illustrates Parisians' fears as the weekend approaches. One man visiting Gollety's shop, a 58-year-old finance worker who did not want to be identified, said he had researched self-defence options, although he had ultimately not bought anything on this occasion. "Given what happened last week and the risk it happens again next weekend, I would prefer to be sensible and protect myself," he said, adding he had had a longstanding feeling of being unsafe. "I've been thinking about this for a long time and I think I'm going to take some steps," he said. Elsewhere in Paris, Yvan Weiss, who owns a finance consulting firm, told Reuters he was taking steps to avoid his shop's windows being broken. Asked if he considered getting pepper spray or other defensive gear, he said he had thought about it but in the end decided to get mechanical metal shutters for his shopfront instead.

item.title: Ex-FBI officials charged with lying to Congress about Hunter Biden probes
item.description: The US Justice Department has charged two former senior FBI officials with lying to Congress about their knowledge of investigations into former President Joe Biden's son, Hunter, according to court documents made public on Friday.
item.dc:creator: Andrew Goudsward
item.content:encoded: The US Justice Department has charged two former senior FBI officials with lying to Congress about their knowledge of investigations into former President Joe Biden's son, Hunter, according to court documents made public on Friday. Nikki Floris, 46, and Bradley Benavides, 56, who each held senior counterintelligence roles at the FBI, were charged in federal court in Washington. They allegedly misled a House of Representatives panel about the role of an FBI foreign influence task force in investigations into Hunter Biden, according to a criminal complaint. The case marks the [USN:L6N3YE1CB TEXT:"latest attempt"] by the Justice Department to investigate and prosecute US officials over incidents that angered President Donald Trump and his allies. Floris and Benavides served in leading roles on the FBI foreign influence task force, a group aimed at combating attempts to influence US elections that was disbanded during the second Trump administration after facing criticism from Republicans. The officials briefed two Republican senators in 2020, warning them of US intelligence concerns that some allegations against Hunter Biden were part of a Russian influence operation, according to prior media reports. Lawyers for Floris condemned the case on Friday as the latest in a string of politically motivated prosecutions by the DOJ under the Trump administration. "The government’s reasons for charging Nikki are as transparent as they are unjust: to push a false narrative for a shot at political points," Floris' lawyers said in a statement. A lawyer for Benavides did not immediately respond to a request for comment. "Lying to Congress by anyone strikes at the heart of our democratic system, but when senior FBI agents lie to Congress believing they are above the law, it’s time to bring the hammer of justice down on them," US Attorney for the District of Columbia Jeanine Pirro wrote in a social media post. Floris and Benavides made an initial court appearance on Friday. A federal grand jury in Washington will have to approve an indictment for the case to move forward. A TRUMP GRIEVANCE The case centers on an issue that has long been a focus of Trump and his allies: the FBI's handling of a laptop purportedly belonging to Hunter Biden that surfaced in the weeks leading up to the 2020 election, which Trump lost to Joe Biden. The criminal complaint alleges that Floris and Benavides lied to the House Judiciary Committee in 2023 testimony where they each claimed little knowledge of the Hunter Biden investigation and the laptop episode. It alleges that Floris and Benavides were in contact with members of the Hunter Biden investigative team in 2020 and took part in the FBI's response to public reporting on the laptop. Benavides told the House panel that he learned about the Hunter Biden probes through searching on Wikipedia, according to the complaint. Hunter Biden was later charged with federal [USN:L1N38C1OP TEXT:"gun and tax-related crimes"] during his father's administration. Joe Biden [USN:S0N3HW02C TEXT:"pardoned his son"] shortly before leaving office. Trump and his allies have [USN:L1N34O1PW TEXT:"long claimed"] that the FBI, during Trump's first term, and social media companies, suppressed the laptop story to protect Joe Biden's campaign. The case against Floris and Benavides does not make that allegation. The DOJ under Trump has also investigated the [USN:L1N41O0U1 TEXT:"US intelligence community's finding"] that Russia sought to aid Trump's 2016 campaign and the FBI raid of Trump's Mar-a-Lago resort for classified documents in 2022. That probe has been [USN:L6N4521BD TEXT:"mired in staff turmoil"]. The DOJ has also brought charges against former FBI Director James Comey for allegedly lying to Congress about media leaks, a case that was later dismissed, and for allegedly threatening Trump in a social media post that featured seashells arranged to form the numbers "86 47."

item.title: Bristol Myers discloses patient death in early-stage cell therapy study
item.description: Bristol Myers Squibb on Friday disclosed a patient death in an early-stage trial studying its experimental CAR-T cell therapy.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Bristol Myers Squibb (BMY.N) on Friday disclosed a patient death in an early-stage trial studying its experimental CAR-T cell therapy. Shares of the drugmaker were trading 2% lower in early trading. The company said a patient with highly active relapsing multiple sclerosis, a central nervous system autoimmune condition, died of septic pneumonia. The patient was a participant in the trial of Bristol Myers' experimental cell therapy zolacabtagene autoleucel, or zola-cel, that is designed to target CD19, a protein found on certain cells that are believed to play a role in autoimmune diseases. After receiving a high-dose of a type of chemotherapy, the patient developed septic pneumonia and died the next day, 44 days after the CAR-T infusion. The patient had delayed motor symptoms that did not respond to treatment with corticosteroids or intravenous immunoglobulin. In September, the company said it was implementing a [USN:L6N44T08D TEXT:"voluntary pause"] on studies for zola-cel, "out of an abundance of caution" as it reviews safety data, after Novartis (NOVN.S) paused eight clinical trials of an experimental cell therapy, called rap-cel. Bristol's early-stage trial enrolled 66 patients, 30 of whom had highly active relapsing MS, and the rest had progressive forms of the disease. In MS, the immune system attacks the protective sheath that covers nerve fibers, known as myelin, which interrupts communication between the brain and the rest of the body. The company said majority of the side effects were brief and reversible, generally consistent with the previously reported zola-cel data. In the study, 42.4% of patients had cytokine release syndrome events, a systemic inflammatory response triggered by an overactivation of the immune system. Five patients experienced immune effector cell-associated neurotoxicity syndrome, a neurological disorder caused by inflammation, but was resolved in about two days. A patient with a progressive form of MS experienced a severe form of the neurotoxicity event, which was treated and resolved within four days. No additional severe side effects have been reported across all zola-cel programs in autoimmune diseases, which include 190 patients treated in early studies, the company said.

item.title: US Justice Dept sues to block possible Alaska election of Democrat to Senate
item.description: The US Justice Department on Thursday sued to preemptively block Alaska from certifying the results of its US Senate race if the Republican incumbent candidate loses by a narrow margin, saying voters could be confused because two Republicans on the ballot have almost identical names.
item.dc:creator: Jan Wolfe
item.content:encoded: The US Justice Department on Thursday sued to preemptively block Alaska from certifying the results of its US Senate race if the Republican incumbent candidate loses by a narrow margin, saying voters could be confused because two Republicans on the ballot have almost identical names. President Donald Trump's administration has taken an increasingly aggressive approach to election oversight, pressing states for voter-registration data and arguing that stricter measures are needed to ensure public confidence in the vote. Critics, including both Democratic and some Republican election officials, view the moves as federal overreach. Control of the US Senate could come down to Alaska, where incumbent Republican Senator Dan S. Sullivan is running a closely contested race against Democrat Mary Peltola. The Justice Department's lawsuit , filed in federal court in Anchorage, takes issue with the presence of a third contender in the race, another Republican named Dan J. Sullivan Jr, alleging he is running "with the intention of misleading supporters of Senator Sullivan into voting for him." The lawsuit asks a federal judge to block the certification of an outcome "that may be impacted by voter confusion," so that there can be "an investigation to determine whether votes cast for Daniel J. Sullivan were meant to be cast for Senator Sullivan." Election law experts have panned the Justice Department's lawsuit, calling it a publicity stunt by President Donald Trump's administration that seeks relief not allowed under federal law. "In short, like many Department letters over the last few years, it is designed to win the press release rather than the litigation," wrote Notre Dame law professor Derek Muller in a blog post , adding that "the legal argument is one of the worst ones I’ve ever seen." The unelected Sullivan, a former US Forest Service worker and elementary school teacher, filed to run as a candidate on May 29 seeking to unseat Senator Dan S. Sullivan and "put Alaska first," according to his campaign website, which advertised "Dan Sullivan Challenges Dan Sullivan for US Senate Seat." Dan J. Sullivan has denied in interviews with US news outlets that his aim is to cause confusion or divert votes from Dan S. Sullivan. The Alaska Supreme Court in June permitted the unelected Sullivan to appear on the ballot. He will appear without a party designation next to his name, while the senator will be listed as the Republican incumbent. Polling has shown Peltola, a former US representative, tied or slightly ahead in Alaska, a state the president carried by some 14 percentage points in 2024. In Alaska, as in much of the US, Trump's approval rating is underwater, hit by rising diesel and gasoline prices and a conflict in the Middle East that has proven deeply unpopular with voters. Public opinion polls suggest Republicans may lose control of one or both houses of Congress, which would likely limit Trump's ability to enact his policies in the final two years of his presidency.

item.title: US authorizes emergency release of up to 400,000 oil barrels from strategic reserve
item.description: The US Department of Energy said on Friday it had authorized an emergency exchange of up to 400,000 barrels of crude oil from the Strategic Petroleum Reserve to address a supply disruption affecting Phillips 66's Lake Charles refinery in Louisiana.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: The US Department of Energy said on Friday it had authorized an emergency exchange of up to 400,000 barrels of crude oil from the Strategic Petroleum Reserve to address a supply disruption affecting Phillips 66's Lake Charles refinery in Louisiana. The SPR is already at [USN:L1N44M0EQ TEXT:"the lowest level"] since 1982 after President Donald Trump tapped it as the US war on Iran disrupted supply lines, and after his predecessor, President Joe Biden, turned to it following Russia's full-scale invasion of Ukraine . The Lake Charles refinery has a capacity to refine about 264,000 barrels per day. The exchange will "help offset temporary disruptions affecting crude oil deliveries to the refinery and support continued production of transportation fuels serving Louisiana and surrounding markets," the department said. The refinery will receive crude oil from the US Strategic Petroleum Reserve, a Phillips 66 spokesperson confirmed on Friday, but he declined to comment on refinery operations or commercial activity. "We do not anticipate impacts to Lake Charles operations," he said.

item.title: Wells Fargo, Intuit latest companies to object to their shares being tokenized, document shows
item.description: Six more companies, including Wells Fargo , Arm Holdings and Intuit , will not allow their shares to be tokenized on a joint trading platform backed by crypto exchange OKX and Intercontinental Exchange , according to a regulatory document seen by Reuters.
item.dc:creator: Hannah Lang
item.content:encoded: Six more companies, including Wells Fargo (WFC.N) , Arm Holdings and Intuit (INTU.O) , will not allow their shares to be tokenized on a joint trading platform backed by crypto exchange OKX and Intercontinental Exchange (ICE.N) , according to a regulatory document seen by Reuters. The new objections, which have not been previously reported, underscore the growing challenges for tokenization, the creation of digital tokens that represent a stock and can be traded on a blockchain similar to cryptocurrencies, despite the US securities regulator recently approving the novel products. In total, 22 companies have objected, according to the document, which outlines the rules of the OKXICE venture and which companies have objected. It does not say why the companies objected. Sixteen of the companies, including Microsoft (MSFT.O) and Alphabet (GOOGL.O) , are listed on Nasdaq (NDAQ.O) . The others are listed on the New York Stock Exchange, which ICE owns. Nasdaq [USN:L4N3ZX156 TEXT:"has teamed up with Payward"], the parent of crypto exchange Kraken, to launch its own tokenized stock platform next year. A spokesperson for Arm did not immediately provide comment. Spokespeople for Wells Fargo and Intuit declined to comment. TOKENIZATION ADVOCATES TOUT 24/7 TRADING The cryptocurrency industry has said stock tokenization could revolutionize markets by allowing shares to be traded 24/7 and settled instantly. OKX and ICE had planned to tokenize 63 stocks [USN:L6N45R063 TEXT:"through their joint venture"], but have encountered objections from issuers. OKX and ICE filed with the US Securities and Exchange Commission earlier this month to launch tokenized stocks under the agency's new [USN:L1N4470NU TEXT:"innovation exemption"]. The exemption allows platforms that facilitate trading of tokenized stocks to operate without complying with many requirements that apply to traditional stock exchanges. Under the exemption, platforms must notify companies before listing tokenized versions of their stocks, and cannot proceed if the issuer objects. Speaking to reporters this week, Andrew Cuomo, co-chairman of the OKXICE joint venture, said given how revolutionary tokenization could be, it was natural for companies to take a "wait and see" approach, CoinDesk reported. While Nasdaq says it welcomes tokenization in principle, it has said such products should be subject to the existing set of rules and investor protections. It has warned that if improperly regulated, tokenization could fragment liquidity and undermine price discovery, among other issues. "Given the risks we believe issuers must be cautious about their participation," the company warned in a September FAQ. A Nasdaq spokesperson pointed Reuters to its FAQ. Although many overseas [USN:L6N3UW0SJ TEXT:"tokenized stocks"] are marketed like stocks, they rarely offer the same rights, disclosures and protections as traditional equities. Under the SEC's exemption, tokenized stocks must confer the same rights and privileges as traditional securities, including the ability to receive dividends and exercise voting rights.

item.title: Acht Bundesländer machen Front gegen Reiches Offshore-Wind-Pläne

Auch das "Handelsblatt" hatte darüber berichtet.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Acht Ministerpräsidentinnen und -präsidenten verschiedener Parteien fordern von Bundeswirtschaftsministerin Katherina Reiche (CDU) deutliche Änderungen an der geplanten Reform der Windenergie auf See. Damit bekräftigen sie Forderungen des Bundesrats, der sich bereits Mitte Oktober gegen zentrale Bestimmungen des Gesetzentwurfs ausgesprochen hatte. Die Regierungschefs warnen Reiche vor einer Gefährdung des Ausbaus der Offshore-Windenergie und negativen Folgen für die deutsche Industrie, wie aus ihrem gemeinsamen Schreiben an die Wirtschaftsministerin hervorgeht, das der Nachrichtenagentur Reuters vorliegt. Auch das "Handelsblatt" hatte darüber berichtet. Ungewöhnlich ist vor allem die Zusammensetzung der acht Länderchefs: Neben den betroffenen Küstenländern Niedersachsen, Schleswig-Holstein, Mecklenburg-Vorpommern sowie Hamburg und Bremen haben auch die Ministerpräsidenten des Saarlands, Bayerns, Nordrhein-Westfalens und Baden-Württembergs den Brief unterzeichnet. Reiche bekommt nun Druck aus der gesamten Republik und von SPD, CDU, CSU und den Grünen. Dass auch etwa Bayern jetzt für Änderungen eintritt, liegt daran, dass die Industrie im Süden enormen Bedarf an umweltfreundlichem Strom hat. Zudem rückt die Lieferung von Offshore-Windstrom nach Süden näher: Die sogenannte SuedLink-Verbindung soll planmäßig ab Ende 2028 Strom nach Bayern liefern können. Die Bundesregierung hatte den Entwurf des Windenergie-auf-See-Gesetzes im September beschlossen. Der Bundestag hat darüber in erster Lesung beraten. Sie sähen im weiteren Gesetzgebungsverfahren "dringenden Handlungsbedarf", mahnen die Ministerpräsidenten nun aber. Es bestehe die Sorge, dass falsche politische Entscheidungen einer Deindustrialisierung Vorschub leisteten. Sie warnen in dem Brief vor dem Verlust von 23.000 der 49.000 Arbeitsplätze und einem Umsatzausfall von 24 Milliarden Euro im Offshore-Wind-Bereich. Die Länder verlangen vor allem eine Möglichkeit für Unternehmen, bereits ersteigerte Offshore-Flächen zurückzugeben, wenn die Windparkprojekte wirtschaftlich nicht mehr realisierbar sind. Die Flächen müssten anschließend zügig neu ausgeschrieben werden können. Zudem lehnen die Länderchefs das im Gesetzentwurf vorgesehene zweistufige Ausschreibungsverfahren ab. Demnach sollen Windparkflächen zunächst ohne staatliche Preisabsicherung vergeben werden. Erst wenn dies scheitert, kommen sogenannte Differenzverträge zum Einsatz. Sie sichern den Betreibern einen bestimmten Strompreis zu und sollen damit Investitionsrisiken begrenzen. "Die vorgesehene Zweistufigkeit ist schädlich und sollte ersatzlos gestrichen werden", heißt es in dem Brief. Der Bundesrat hatte bereits am 16. Oktober die Streichung der entsprechenden Gesetzesbestimmung verlangt. Die Länderkammer begründete dies mit hohen Marktpreisrisiken für die Betreiber und dadurch steigenden Finanzierungskosten. Zugleich forderte sie die Bundesregierung auf, eine Rückgabe wirtschaftlich nicht mehr tragfähiger Projekte und die anschließende Neuvergabe der Flächen zu prüfen. Die Offshore-Windindustrie steht ohnehin unter Druck, weil stark gestiegene Finanzierungs-, Material- und Projektkosten nicht mehr zu den Ausschreibungsbedingungen passen. So waren die für dieses Jahr geplanten Ausschreibungen für Windparks auf See ausgesetzt und auf 2027 verschoben worden, nachdem sich im August 2025 keine Bieter fanden. Für zwei Nordseeflächen mit einer geplanten Leistung von insgesamt 2,5 Gigawatt ging bei der Bundesnetzagentur kein einziges Gebot ein. Die Ministerpräsidenten dringen auf eine rasche Reform, damit 2027 wieder erfolgreiche Ausschreibungen möglich werden. "Das Ziel von 70 Gigawatt bis 2045 muss als verlässliche Perspektive bestehen bleiben", heißt es in dem Brief.

item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Die Ukraine und Russland haben einer lokalen Feuerpause für die von russischen Truppen besetzte Stadt Oleschky zugestimmt. Sie solle am 29. Oktober beginnen, teilte das US-Präsidialamt am Freitag mit. Nach Angaben des Weißen Hauses hat die First Lady der USA, Melania Trump, das Abkommen zwischen den beiden Ländern vermittelt. Es sei vereinbart worden, sämtliche Kampfhandlungen in Oleschky vorübergehend einzustellen. Dies solle es ermöglichen, humanitäre Hilfsgüter zu verteilen und Zivilisten über einen dafür vorgesehenen sicheren Korridor in Sicherheit zu bringen. Der ukrainische Verhandlungsführer Dawyd Arachamija erklärte, die Vereinbarung sei das Ergebnis eines langen Prozesses, an dem neben Melania Trump auch Papst Leo beteiligt gewesen sei. Der Kreml bestätigte am Freitag die Vereinbarung und teilte mit, das russische und ukrainische Militär arbeiteten daran, die Termine für die Umsetzung festzulegen. Das russische Präsidialamt hatte bereits Anfang der Woche erklärt, dass an einer Verbesserung der Lage gearbeitet werde, nachdem Präsident Wladimir Putin dem Papst seine Kooperationsbereitschaft signalisiert hatte. Sprecher Dmitri Peskow sagte, alle Zivilisten, die Oleschky verlassen wollten, dürften dies tun. Die Evakuierung werde voraussichtlich mehrere Tage dauern. Peskow würdigte die Rolle von Melania Trump, die bei einem Telefonat zwischen dem russischen Präsidenten Wladimir Putin und US-Präsident Donald Trump besprochen worden sei. "Die Lage in Oleschky ist katastrophal", erklärte Melania Trump in einer Mitteilung. Die Stadt an der Front stehe vor dem Kollaps. Die verbliebene Bevölkerung bestehe vor allem aus älteren Menschen, die dringend medizinische Hilfe, Medikamente, Lebensmittel und sauberes Trinkwasser benötigten. Die Feuerpause soll es unbewaffneten Teams beider Länder ermöglichen, die Bewohner in ihren Häusern aufzusuchen und den Transport für diejenigen zu koordinieren, die die Stadt verlassen wollten. US-FERNSEHTEAM SOLL EVAKUIERUNG DOKUMENTIEREN Diejenigen, die in Sicherheit gebracht werden möchten, erhielten koordinierte Unterstützung und Transportmittel zu ihrem gewünschten Ziel, sagte die First Lady. "Ich gehe davon aus, dass einige nach Russland und andere in die Ukraine ausreisen wollen." Die Evakuierung soll von einer US-Medienorganisation dokumentiert werden. Der konservative US-Sender Newsmax berichtete, er habe für seine Kameras exklusiven Zugang erhalten, um den Einsatz zu begleiten. Oleschky liegt gegenüber von Cherson auf der anderen Seite des Flusses Dnipro und ist seit Februar 2022 von russischen Truppen besetzt. US-Angaben zufolge leben dort noch etwa 1700 bis 2000 Menschen, darunter rund 50 Kinder. Vor dem Krieg hatte die Stadt rund 24.000 Einwohner. Zudem waren etwa 90 Prozent des Stadtgebiets nach der Zerstörung des Kachowka-Staudamms überschwemmt worden. Melania Trump und ihr Vertreter verhandelten demnach direkt mit der russischen und der ukrainischen Führung über die Bedingungen der Waffenruhe. Die First Lady hatte sich bereits für die Rückkehr ukrainischer Kinder eingesetzt, die während des Krieges von Russland verschleppt worden waren. US-Präsident Donald Trump hatte den ukrainischen Präsidenten Wolodymyr Selenskyj zuletzt zu einer Einigung mit dem russischen Präsidenten Wladimir Putin gedrängt, um den im Februar 2022 begonnenen Krieg zu beenden.
