item.title: India's Scotch probe of Diageo, Pernod undermining India-UK pact benefits, trade group says
item.description: India's move to exclude bulk Scotch imports from a reduced 75% tariff goes against provisions agreed in an India-UK trade deal, a group representing liquor makers Diageo and Pernod Ricard wrote in a letter seen by Reuters.
item.dc:creator: Aditya Kalra
item.content:encoded: India's move to exclude bulk Scotch imports from a reduced 75% tariff goes against provisions agreed in an India-UK trade deal, a group representing liquor makers Diageo and Pernod Ricard wrote in a letter seen by Reuters. Whisky tariffs were a sticking point during the years of protracted negotiations leading up to the deal's July 15 implementation, though India ultimately agreed to halve import taxes on certain Scotch imports from 150% to 75% immediately and to 40% over 10 years. The British government said "iconic UK products" like whiskies would benefit from the pact. Indian investigators, however, have privately told companies the reduced rate does not apply to bulk Scotch concentrates, creating the first significant dispute over the free trade agreement since it took effect. India's Directorate of Revenue Intelligence [USN:L4N4650OU TEXT:"searched the offices"] of Pernod (PERP.PA) and Diageo (DGE.L) and questioned executives this month as part of an investigation into whether they misclassified imported products to benefit from the reduced rate. In a letter to the commerce minister on Friday, the International Spirits and Wines Association of India (ISWAI) wrote that the classification issue "risks undermining, in practice, an important market-access benefit negotiated and agreed between India and the United Kingdom." "The preferential tariff treatment negotiated ... could effectively become unavailable for these imports," continued the letter, a copy of which was seen by Reuters. ISWAI declined to comment on its letter, while India's commerce ministry did not immediately respond. Pernod, which counts India as its biggest market by volume, declined to comment, and Diageo did not respond to a request for comment. Both told Reuters earlier this week that they were cooperating with Indian authorities carrying out the investigation. BIG IMPLICATIONS FOR INDIA'S DRINKS SECTOR Import tariff disputes have long been a [USN:L4N3P10W5 TEXT:"sore point"] for foreign investors in India, who have in the past faced demands for large amounts of back-tax. Such disputes have embroiled the likes of Samsung and Volkswagen. Pernod is already facing antitrust cases in India and a $314 million back-tax demand from Indian authorities, who accuse it of undervaluing some imports. The company denies wrongdoing. ISWAI's letter underscores the shockwaves the investigation has sent through India's $65 billion alcohol market. Britain accounts for almost 75% of India's imported spirits, primarily driven by Scotch whisky, according to Crisil Ratings. Indian government inspectors have told companies that they do not benefit from the reduced 75% tariff on bulk imports of Scotch concentrates, which must be declared under a customs classification that attracts a 150% duty, three people with direct knowledge of the matter told Reuters. Pernod and Diageo import bulk concentrates, mixing them with other ingredients to produce hugely popular Indian brands like Royal Stag, Blenders Pride and McDowell’s. The three people said companies including Diageo and Pernod believe concentrates imported from Britain should benefit from the new, lower tariff. And ISWAI said in its letter that the India–UK agreement expressly provides preferential tariff treatment for whisky under the relevant tariff lines. An urgent clarification could ensure market-access benefits negotiated by India and Britain are realised "while avoiding uncertainty and disruption for legitimate industry participants," the letter said. A spokesperson for the British government said: "We are working with the Government of India to resolve this issue to ensure UK businesses can export under the tariffs agreed in the trade deal."

item.title: Fast-fashion group Shein agrees to pay $100 million to settle US FTC probe
item.description: Chinese fast-fashion giant Shein has agreed to pay $100 million to settle an investigation by the US Federal Trade Commission over delivery delays and other customer complaints, a source with direct knowledge told Reuters on Friday.
item.dc:creator: Helen Reid, Jody Godoy
item.content:encoded: Chinese fast-fashion giant Shein (0625.HK) has agreed to pay $100 million to settle an investigation by the US Federal Trade Commission over delivery delays and other customer complaints, a source with direct knowledge told Reuters on Friday. The settlement, equivalent to 44% of Shein's second-quarter [USN:L4N45K0YB TEXT:"profit"], is the latest to hit the online fast-fashion retailer facing a regulatory and tax [USN:L6N42Y0OM TEXT:"crackdown"] in Europe and the US that has slammed the brakes on its growth. Shein, founded in China though headquartered in Singapore, said in a statement to Reuters that it had "reached a constructive outcome with the FTC", and that additional information would be shared soon. An FTC spokesperson declined to comment. The company had warned in July filings for its Hong Kong IPO that the US [USN:L6N43U12W TEXT:"probe"] could lead to significant fines. Consumers filed more than 12,000 complaints about Shein over more than $11 million in purchases between January 2020 and June 2026, according to FTC records reviewed by Reuters. At least some of those relate to shipping, with customers reporting to the FTC and Better Business Bureau that they never received packages that Shein had marked as delivered, and that Shein customer service did not resolve the issue. Reuters was not able to independently verify the substance of the complaints, or whether they were ultimately resolved. As well as selling its own-brand clothing, Shein's website also operates as a marketplace where third-party sellers offer everything from toys to household appliances and decor. MORE PAIN AHEAD FOR SHEIN WITH HIGHER EU FEES Shein shares have already dropped 22% from their September 1 listing price as investors realised the extent to which the European Union's €3 [USN:L6N42Y0OM TEXT:"fees"] on low-value e-commerce packages have bruised its business there. And there's further pain ahead for Shein, with the EU imposing an additional €2 handling fee from November 1, making the total fee €5 per separate customs code. "The way these tariffs are implemented is extra punishing for Shein," said Mike Ryan, head of e-commerce insights at Smarter Ecommerce, who has tracked how Shein has dialled down its spending on Google Ads visibility in Europe. Shein was known for selling $5 dresses and $10 jeans, but has been forced to raise its prices as the US and then Europe closed customs duty loopholes. CEO Sky Xu said last month that Shein would develop more higher-priced brands in an attempt to boost profitability. Shein is also still under [USN:L8N3ZC0X6 TEXT:"investigation"] by the European Commission over illegal products on its marketplace. It was fined [USN:L1N3UQ0XG TEXT:"€150 million"] ($168 million) by France's data protection authority over the improper use of cookies last year. It's not the first time the US FTC has taken action against online retailers over deliveries. US firm Fashion Nova was fined $9.3 million in 2020 for failing to meet shipping promises to customers and giving them gift cards instead of refunds. Crocs Inc-owned Hey Dude was also fined $1.95 million in 2023 for failing to notify customers of shipping delays and suppressing negative reviews. ($1 = 0.8928 euros)

item.title: Storm causes power outages and traffic disruptions in France and Britain
item.description: Storm Austen cut power to nearly 300,000 French homes and disrupted train and plane services with heavy winds and rain on Friday, while also knocking out electricity for some 12,000 homes in Britain.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Storm Austen cut power to nearly 300,000 French homes and disrupted train and plane services with heavy winds and rain on Friday, while also knocking out electricity for some 12,000 homes in Britain. A low-pressure front brought 111 mph (179 kph) winds and rains across Europe overnight with towns facing power outages as trees and debris littered roads, causing traffic issues, airport and train delays and reduced access to bridges. Utility Enedis said in a situation update on Friday that nearly 300,000 clients had no electricity from the storm, with most of disruptions located in Brittany on the western coast and Normandy in the north. Britain's National Grid said engineers had to restore power to more than 12,000 homes. Major disruptions were expected on the Paris commuter rail services, while all rail traffic was suspended in Normandy, French transport minister Philippe Tabarot said in a post on X. Disruptions were also underway at airports, with flights diverted from the main Paris hub Charles de Gaulle to Orly airport, and diversions to other French and European airports anticipated, he added. Meteo France, France's weather agency, has issued orange alerts for much of the country's northwest, saying that heavy wind and thunderstorms would continue into late Friday. A second storm named Boelo is expected to impact Northern Ireland, Scotland and parts of northern England over the weekend, Britain's Met Office said. Heavy rain is expected to move from the west through Saturday as wind strength builds with gusts between 70 mph and and 80 mph in exposed areas, the Met office said.

item.title: Russia, Ukraine agree to ceasefire in Ukrainian city hit by food crisis, brokered by Melania Trump
item.description: US first lady Melania Trump has secured a ceasefire between Russia and Ukraine in the Russian-controlled city of Oleshky, which will begin next Thursday, the White House said on Friday.
item.dc:creator: Steve Holland, Ryan Patrick Jones
item.content:encoded: US first lady Melania Trump has secured a ceasefire between Russia and Ukraine in the Russian-controlled city of Oleshky, which will begin next Thursday, the White House said on Friday. The chief of staff of Russian forces, Valery Gerasimov, said on the Defence Ministry's Telegram channel that Russian troops would halt fire from 4 a.m. local time (0100 GMT) on Tuesday to allow for the humanitarian operation to start. Residents of the southern Ukrainian city, occupied by Russian forces since February 2022, have reported a deepening food [USN:L8N45K1N1 TEXT:"crisis"]. "Both nations agreed to temporarily stop all military action in Oleshky to allow for humanitarian aid to enter and to prepare a civilian evacuation through a designated safe passageway," a White House statement said. Ukraine's top negotiator, David Arakhamia, said on Telegram that the humanitarian operation would start once a ceasefire was in place. He said the accord, the result of a long process involving Melania Trump and Pope Leo, would set up a humanitarian corridor for residents to leave and allow assistance into the town. In Moscow, the Kremlin welcomed the agreement. It praised Melania Trump's role in securing the agreement and said President Donald Trump and Russian President Vladimir Putin had discussed details. The Kremlin said earlier this week that work was under way to ease the humanitarian situation in Oleshky after Putin told the pope he was ready to cooperate on the issue. The development comes as President Trump pressures Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskiy to reach an agreement with Putin to end the war, which began when Russia invaded Ukraine in 2022. FIRST LADY HAS SOUGHT TO HELP UKRAINIAN CHILDREN Melania Trump has been active in trying to get Ukrainian children seized by Russia during the war returned to their families. "The situation in Oleshky is dire. Oleshky is a front-line war city on the brink of disaster. Oleshky's remaining population is comprised primarily of elderly residents who urgently need medical attention, medicine, food, and clean water," Melania Trump said in the statement. The ceasefire will allow non-military teams from both countries to visit residents in their homes and coordinate transportation for those wishing to evacuate to either Russia or Ukraine, with an unnamed American media organization accompanying the teams to document the process, the first lady said. Newsmax, a right-leaning news outlet, said in a report that its cameras would be granted "exclusive access to document the effort." Oleshky, located across the Dnipro River from the Ukrainian-held city of Kherson, has a remaining population of 1,700 to 2,000 people — primarily elderly residents, along with about 50 children — down from roughly 24,000 before the war, the White House said. About 90% of the city was flooded following the 2023 destruction of the Kakhovka Dam, according to the White House. The statement said Melania Trump and her representative worked directly with Russian and Ukrainian leadership to define the terms of the localized ceasefire. "Residents who wish to evacuate will receive coordinated support and transportation to their preferred destination. I anticipate some will want to go to Russia, and some to Ukraine,” Melania Trump said.

item.title: Ibovespa oscila perto do zero a zero com expectativa para eleição; Bradesco recua
item.description: O Ibovespa operava perto da estabilidade nesta sexta-feira, a dois dias do segundo turno da eleição presidencial, com o noticiário corporativo destacando o resultado trimestral do Bradesco, que mostrou lucro em linha com as expectativas do mercado, mas piora em dado de inadimplência, o que afetava as ações do banco.
item.dc:creator: Paula Arend Laier
item.content:encoded: O Ibovespa operava perto da estabilidade nesta sexta-feira, a dois dias do segundo turno da eleição presidencial, com o noticiário corporativo destacando o resultado trimestral do Bradesco, que mostrou lucro em linha com as expectativas do mercado, mas piora em dado de inadimplência, o que afetava as ações do banco. Por volta de 12h35, o Ibovespa (.BVSP) , referência do mercado acionário brasileiro, tinha variação positiva de 0,16%, a 204.451,59 pontos, tendo oscilado entre 203.428 e 204.898,52 pontos até o momento. O volume financeiro somava R$14,85 bilhões. Pesquisas eleitorais têm mostrado uma disputa acirrada pelo Palácio do Planalto. Na noite da véspera, o Datafolha mostrou o senador Flávio Bolsonaro (PL) e o presidente Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva (PT) empatados com 50% dos votos válidos. Na semana passada, o placar estava em 51% a 49% a favor de Flávio nos votos válidos, quando não são considerados os votos brancos e nulos e os indecisos. Novos levantamentos estão previstos para o sábado, mas antes o foco deve ficar no debate entre os candidatos na noite desta sexta-feira, na TV Globo. "Independentemente de quem vencer, o próximo governo precisará lidar com o aumento da dívida pública, o elevado endividamento das famílias e a desaceleração do crescimento econômico", afirmou relatório da Oxford Economics nesta sexta-feira. "A aprovação de reformas relevantes exigirá negociações com o bloco de centro do Congresso. Embora um governo (de Flávio) Bolsonaro possa ter maior espaço político para avançar com reformas, sua agenda econômica e sua capacidade de obter apoio parlamentar permanecem incertas, especialmente na Câmara dos Deputados. Caso Lula seja reeleito, a governabilidade poderá ser mais desafiadora diante do aumento da representação do partido de (Flávio) Bolsonaro no Senado." Agentes financeiros aguardam forte volatilidade na bolsa na segunda-feira, independentemente do desfecho da eleição. No primeiro turno, liderado por Flávio, o Ibovespa fechou em alta de 7,7%. Parte do movimento decorreu da expectativa de que uma mudança em Brasília vai melhorar as perspectivas fiscais para o país, mesmo com a visão de que não será um trabalho fácil. Outubro tem registrado uma recuperação do fluxo de capital externo, com uma entrada líquida de R$20,157 bilhões até o dia 21, puxado principalmente por um fluxo positivo de R$10 bilhões apenas no dia 5, no primeiro pregão após o primeiro turno. A pauta macroeconômica no Brasil ainda mostrou que o Índice Nacional de Preços ao Consumidor Amplo 15 ( IPCA-15 ) teve alta de 0,32% em outubro sobre o mês anterior, após aumento de 0,70% em setembro, acumulando alta de 4,62% em 12 meses. Economistas esperavam avanço de 0,43% na comparação mensal e alta de 4,73% em 12 meses, segundo pesquisa da Reuters. No cenário internacional, a semana terminava com o S&P 500 (.SPX) , uma das referências do mercado acionário norte-americano, em queda de 0,13%, enquanto o rendimento do título de 10 anos do Tesouro dos Estados Unidos marcava 5,00%, de 4,95% na véspera. O barril do petróleo Brent avançava 2,56%, a US$116,07. DESTAQUES BRADESCO PN recuava 0,45%, após divulgar lucro líquido recorrente de R$7,1 bilhões no terceiro trimestre, alta de 14,6% em relação ao mesmo período do ano passado, em linha com as previsões no mercado. A carteira de crédito aumentou de 11,1% ano a ano, enquanto o índice de inadimplência acima de 90 dias ficou em 4,6%, de 4,1% um ano antes. O presidente-executivo do Bradesco, Marcelo Noronha, afirmou nesta sexta-feira que observa uma pressão na inadimplência e no crédito no sistema financeiro no país. Na mínima, mais cedo, o papel chegou a cair quase 2,9%. ITAÚ UNIBANCO PN cedia 0,19%, acompanhado por SANTANDER BRASIL UNIT , em queda de 1,48%. BANCO DO BRASIL ON (BBAS3.SA) subia 0,96% e BTG PACTUAL UNIT mostrava acréscimo de 0,11%. PETROBRAS PN avançava 2,37%, endossada pelo movimento do preço do petróleo no exterior. Na noite da véspera, a estatal disse que avalia positivamente a decisão da Agência Nacional do Petróleo (ANP) de postergar para 19 de novembro a realização da audiência pública sobre o Programa de Redução da Concentração no Mercado de Gás Natural ( Gas Release ). VALE ON (VALE3.SA) valorizava-se 0,57%. CSN ON (CSNA3.SA) subia 2,22%, em pregão sem direção comum no setor, após fortes perdas na véspera. USIMINAS PNA mostrava acréscimo de 0,47% e GERDAU PN (GGBR4.SA) recuava 0,16%. TELEFÔNICA BRASIL ON (VIVT3.SA) , que opera sob a marca Vivo, caía 2,71%, em pregão negativo no setor. TIM ON (TIMS3.SA) perdia 1,79%. EMBRAER ON (EMBJ3.SA) mostrava declínio de 0,33%, após divulgar nesta sexta-feira que sua carteira de pedidos consolidada atingiu US$35,7 bilhões no terceiro trimestre, crescimento de 14% na comparação anual e ultrapassando o recorde histórico registrado no trimestre anterior.

item.title: Safety company acknowledges hack seven months after breach exposed millions of crime tips
item.description: Safety company Navigate360 on Friday acknowledged hackers had broken into one of its systems and copied months' worth of data, seven months after a widely publicized breach exposed millions of crime tips.
item.dc:creator: Raphael Satter
item.content:encoded: Safety company Navigate360 on Friday acknowledged hackers had broken into one of its systems and copied months' worth of data, seven months after a widely publicized breach exposed millions of crime tips. In a statement, Navigate360 said names, addresses, dates of birth, Social Security numbers and other sensitive information had potentially been exposed. Here are some details: In March, a hacker calling themselves "Internet Yiff Machine" said they had broken into tip intelligence platform P3 Global Intel, an arm of Navigate360, and [USN:L6N40615S TEXT:"stolen 93 gigabytes of data"], including 8 million confidential tips. At the time, Navigate360 said it was investigating "whether we have experienced an incident" and declined further comment. In recent days, government officials in places such as Nevada and Canada have been quoted in the media as saying Navigate360 had only given them partial information about the breach despite repeated requests. Police forces in Ontario suspended their use of the service after a Canadian Broadcasting Corporation report found that hundreds of thousands of Canadian tipsters had been exposed in the breach. Navigate360 did not immediately respond to a Reuters question seeking additional details about the hack or the timing of its announcement.

item.title: Building collapses in Kenyan capital, rescuers on the scene
item.description: A 12-storey building under construction in Kenya's capital Nairobi collapsed on Friday, and a Reuters witness said rescuers were on the scene.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: A 12-storey building under construction in Kenya's capital Nairobi collapsed on Friday, and a Reuters witness said rescuers were on the scene. The Nairobi County governor's office said in a statement there were reports people may be trapped beneath the rubble. It was not immediately clear what caused the building to collapse. Governor Johnson Sakaja's office said the ground floor of the collapsed building in the Eastleigh neighbourhood was occupied. A Reuters video showed a crowd had gathered at the scene while an excavator moved rubble.

item.title: Soccer club Valencia says group backed by KKR founders buys 42% stake
item.description: Spanish soccer club Valencia CF said on Friday an investment group backed by KKR co-founders George Roberts and Henry Kravis would buy a 42% stake in the club in a deal valuing it at €1.25 billion ($1.4 billion) including debt.
item.dc:creator: Yantoultra Ngui
item.content:encoded: Spanish soccer club Valencia CF said on Friday an investment group backed by KKR co-founders George Roberts and Henry Kravis would buy a 42% stake in the club in a deal valuing it at €1.25 billion ($1.4 billion) including debt. Pitchwise Holdings, a consortium of family offices and long-term institutional investors led by sports executives Ann Rodriguez and Corey Woolfolk, will acquire the shares from majority owner Meriton Holdings, Valencia said. The investors will also inject €100 million into the club, Valencia said, adding that the deal remains subject to customary closing conditions, including regulatory approvals. Meriton will retain a majority stake, while Kiat Lim will remain president. Rodriguez and Woolfolk will join Lim in a new ownership group, Valencia said. The deal comes as wealthy families and institutional investors [USN:L4N43E020 TEXT:"increasingly seek exposure"] to sports franchises, attracted by their global audiences, media rights and commercial growth potential. Pitchwise's backers include Roberts and Kravis, co-founders and co-executive chairmen of KKR, the global investment firm, as well as Penner Sports Group, the Denver-based sports and entertainment holding company founded by Greg and Carrie Penner. Penner Sports Group's holdings include the NFL's Denver Broncos and a minority stake in Major League Baseball's Colorado Rockies, Valencia said. Lim said Pitchwise was selected from several interested parties because of its "long-term investment expertise and sports acumen". Valencia said the valuation reflects its men's and women's teams, the 49,000-seat Mestalla stadium and [USN:L4N3SS0RP TEXT:"the Nou Mestalla project"], which is expected to have capacity for more than 70,000 fans. The new ownership group will oversee the club's move to the Nou Mestalla stadium, which Valencia described as its most significant milestone in 100 years. ($1 = 0.8937 euros)

item.title: LVHM-owned watchmaker Zenith to cut jobs, shift upmarket, source says
item.description: LVMH-owned Swiss watchmaker Zenith has launched a consultation process that could see up to half of its Swiss workforce laid off as it shifts its focus to more profitable luxury watches, a person close to the company said.
item.dc:creator: Alessandro Parodi
item.content:encoded: LVMH-owned (LVMH.PA) Swiss watchmaker Zenith has launched a consultation process that could see up to half of its Swiss workforce laid off as it shifts its focus to more profitable luxury watches, a person close to the company said. Swiss watchmakers have struggled for years with weak demand from inflation-hit consumers and growing competition from smartwatches, with only the most expensive brands proving resilient. "A staff consultation process was initiated today concerning a proposed strategic repositioning of the Maison," Zenith said in a statement on Thursday, without giving further details. Under the plan, Zenith will focus on the high-end segment, drawing on its expertise in complex watch movements, the person said. The segment typically includes watches priced above 3,000 Swiss francs ($3,650). The company could cut up to 100 jobs at its Le Locle plant in Switzerland, around half the workforce there, as well as about 100 positions in international operations, including sales and marketing, the person added. LVMH did not immediately respond to a request for comment. Zenith is one of the smaller watch brands owned by the luxury group. LVMH's Watches and Jewellery division reported 2025 sales of €10.49 billion ($11.74 billion) and profit of €1.51 billion. ($1 = 0.8233 Swiss francs) ($1 = 0.8933 euros)

item.title: UK approves J&J's oral psoriasis pill
item.description: Britain's medicines regulator on Friday approved Johnson & Johnson's daily pill for adults and teenagers with moderate-to-severe plaque psoriasis, a skin condition causing red, scaly and often itchy or painful patches.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Britain's medicines regulator on Friday approved Johnson & Johnson's (JNJ.N) daily pill for adults and teenagers with moderate-to-severe plaque psoriasis, a skin condition causing red, scaly and often itchy or painful patches. Here are some details: The Medicines and Healthcare products Regulatory Agency (MHRA) approved the oral drug Icotyde for people aged 12 and older who weigh at least 40 kg The approval was based on four late-stage trials in 2,500 people with the disease, including 72 teenagers aged 12 to under 18 In all four studies, patients who took the drug saw better results after 16 weeks than those given a placebo, the regulator said Icotyde was [USN:L4N4061MF TEXT:"approved in the US"] earlier this year for the same condition — its first approved indication The drug is made in collaboration with Protagonist Therapeutics (PTGX.O) J&J is also studying the drug, chemically known as icotrokinra, for ulcerative colitis, psoriatic arthritis and Crohn's disease The company expects the treatment to bring in $5 billion in peak sales across multiple indications The drug competes with established psoriasis treatments such as Bristol Myers Squibb's (BMY.N) Sotyktu and AbbVie's blockbuster (ABBV.N) Skyrizi

item.title: Seven killed as gunmen open fire at church in Jordan, authorities say
item.description: Seven people were killed and 34 injured on Friday when gunmen opened fire during a funeral at a church in Jordan's Karak governorate, the head of the country's Public Security Directorate told reporters, in a rare attack on the country's Christian minority.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Seven people were killed and 34 injured on Friday when gunmen opened fire during a funeral at a church in Jordan's Karak governorate, the head of the country's Public Security Directorate told reporters, in a rare attack on the country's Christian minority. Speaking at a press conference in Karak, Major General Abdallah al-Maaytah said most of those wounded in the shooting at the Hamoud Church in Karak were still receiving treatment, and that the hunt for the attackers was ongoing. Interior Minister Mazin Al Farrayeh said the attack had been carried out by "extremists", but that it was too early to tell whether they had any links to known groups either inside or outside Jordan. There was no immediate claim of responsibility. A video aired on Jordan's state-owned Al-Mamlaka television station that appeared to be from a security camera mounted on the church showed three people firing at it from a sidewalk and hiding behind trees and a low wall. The video showed the attackers then running towards the church's entrance. Reuters was able to verify the video from the entry path and wall surrounding the church, as well as other details. Khaled Burqan, who was at the funeral, told Al-Mamlaka that dozens of people were present and that the gunmen opened fire on them for several minutes. Ihab Ammareen, another witness, told the station that he saw bloodied people collapse on the floor after the attack. "People were crying, wailing, screaming — it's hard to describe," he told the station. BLOOD SMEARED ON THE GROUND Jordan's King Abdullah visited Karak hours after the attack and said the perpetrators would be punished "with an iron fist". "The terrorist attack against Karak will be met with the harshest retaliation. Those who delude themselves into thinking that they can divide Jordanians with their bullets have no chance in the face of our unity," he said in a statement. Reuters footage from the church after the attack showed blood smeared on the floor near its entrance, where security forces were deployed. Such attacks are extremely rare in Jordan, which is relatively stable, though Jordanian authorities say they have repeatedly foiled attempted attacks by Islamist militants in recent years. Christians make up a minority of Jordan's population. The country is home to several biblical sites that attract Christian pilgrims from around the world. Jordan's Minister of Endowments and Islamic Affairs Mohammad Khalayleh and several members of Jordan's parliament condemned the attack in comments to Al-Mamlaka. The US ambassador to the United Nations Mike Waltz described it in a post on X as a "depraved and brutal attack on a house of worship." Jordan was among the US allies in the region to be hit by Iranian attacks this year after the US and Israel launched strikes against Iran in February.

item.title: BASF raises Evonik offer to €24 a share, sources say
item.description: BASF has increased its takeover offer for German chemicals manufacturer Evonik Industries to €24 per share, two people close to the deal told Reuters on Friday.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: BASF (BASFn.DE) has increased its takeover offer for German chemicals manufacturer Evonik Industries (EVKn.DE) to €24 per share, two people close to the deal told Reuters on Friday. The offer, increased from an original bid of about €22.15 per share, would value Evonik at around €11.18 billion ($12.51 billion). Evonik had in September [USN:L6N45K0R8 TEXT:"rejected"] BASF's €10.3 billion bid as too low, according to sources. Evonik declined to comment, as did its largest shareholder the RAG Foundation. Bloomberg News first reported on Friday that the German chemicals giant had raised its offer to more than €11 billion, citing people familiar with the matter. BASF's renewed offer comes a day after Evonik's [USN:S8N432008 TEXT:"interest"] in acquiring US specialty chemicals firm Ashland (ASH.N) , valued at around $3.3 billion, surfaced. Evonik's interest in Ashland started before BASF launched its takeover bid, two people familiar with the matter told Reuters. BASF considers an acquisition of Ashland by Evonik to be too risky, according to a source close to the matter. Evonik's shares closed the day 2.7% higher at €21.26, while BASF shares were up 0.15%. JOBS GUARANTEE Evonik's products include high-tech plastics and feed additives as well as ingredients for coatings and household products. BASF makes engineering plastics, super absorbent polymers, vitamins and chemicals for industrial uses. BASF [USN:L6N4680Y0 TEXT:"said"] on Thursday it would honour existing agreements to preserve jobs made by Evonik in the event of an acquisition and warned that more painful takeover approaches from abroad were looming. "Any potential takeover of Evonik must be judged on the basis of the prospects it opens up for the companies, their sites and, above all, for the workforce," Sinischa Horvat, works council chairman at BASF, said in a statement. "For us, one thing is clear: our existing site agreement remains in force. It must not be called into question by a potential takeover, nor must it be undermined by its financing or the resulting costs," he added. The German state of North Rhine-Westphalia, where Evonik is based, said earlier this month that jobs at Evonik and its independent development must not be jeopardised by a takeover. ($1 = 0.8937 euros)

item.title: EU vows to fix 'China Shock 2.0' via talks with Beijing
item.description: The European Union should focus on dialogue with Beijing to curb imports of products such as chemicals and machinery to rein in a damaging trade deficit with China, EU ministers said on Friday, as the bloc considers import quotas for plastics.
item.dc:creator: Philip Blenkinsop, Padraic Halpin
item.content:encoded: The European Union should focus on dialogue with Beijing to curb imports of products such as chemicals and machinery to rein in a damaging trade deficit with China, EU ministers said on Friday, as the bloc considers import quotas for plastics. European Trade Commissioner Maros Sefcovic earlier this month [USN:L6N45V0LF TEXT:"agreed with Beijing"] for the EU to cut imports of hybrid vehicles from China by more than half to address a deficit that has swelled to more than €1 billion ($1.12 billion) a day, and to support Europe's struggling carmakers. Irish Foreign Minister Helen McEntee told a news conference after a ministerial meeting in Dublin that all EU members were determined the Commission should continue dialogue with Beijing "There's a very clear desire for us to move beyond that (hybrid cars) and to look at other areas, chemicals, machinery. There's a number of issues, agrifood sector, and areas that have been mentioned," she said. She added that, while dialogue was the priority, the Commission could use existing trade defence tools itself to resolve some imbalances. Sefcovic told the news conference he had heard every trade minister's views on which sectors should be the next priorities for trade measures. PLASTICS SAFEGUARDS NEXT IN LINE He continued that an investigation into safeguards for plastics appeared to be the next to be launched. "Currently, I think the plastics sector is the closest," he said. "We are looking into whether all the requirements to launch an investigation are in place." He appeared to be referring to a request for measures to curb imports of PET, the plastic widely used in packaging, which [USN:L6N4600W6 TEXT:"lawyers told Reuters"] earlier this month had been submitted. China needs foreign buyers for the flood of relatively cheap state-subsidised goods its own shoppers can't absorb, and the EU is torn between welcoming those imports to ease living costs and keeping them out to rebuild its own factories. The EU's goods trade deficit swelled to more than €370 billion ($414.25 billion) in 2025 and is on course to break well past €400 billion this year, a situation European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen has called "unsustainable". European industry says the export surge, dubbed China Shock 2.0, is already causing factory closures and job losses, most notably the [USN:L8N44W0B8 TEXT:"100,000 positions set to go"] at Volkswagen. China has said in the past it is not the root cause of the EU's problems, but a partner in solving them. European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen said this week there were growing concerns for chemicals and machinery. Lithuania Foreign Minister Kestutis Budrys said on Friday that pharmaceuticals could also be included. France's junior minister for trade, Nicolas Forissier, said dialogue was only possible now that the EU was speaking as one. Chinese authorities "understand when you are clear, when you speak frankly, when you are firm on your positions," he said. ($1 = 0.8914 euros)

item.title: Oro se encamina a caída semanal, alza del crudo refuerza expectativas de un alza de tasas
item.description: El oro tocó el viernes un mínimo de tres meses y se encaminaba a su mayor caída semanal en más de cuatro meses, ya que el aumento de los precios de la energía avivó los temores inflacionarios y reforzó las expectativas de una subida de las tasas de interés en Estados Unidos la próxima semana.
item.dc:creator: Noel John, Anushree Mukherjee
item.content:encoded: El oro tocó el viernes un mínimo de tres meses y se encaminaba a su mayor caída semanal en más de cuatro meses, ya que el aumento de los precios de la energía avivó los temores inflacionarios y reforzó las expectativas de una subida de las tasas de interés en Estados Unidos la próxima semana. * El oro al contado cayó un 0,6% a 4.000,59 dólares la onza a las 1520 GMT tras haber bajado anteriormente por debajo de la barrera de los 4.000 dólares por primera vez desde mediados de julio y haber tocado un mínimo de la sesión de 3.975,23 dólares. * El oro ha caído un 4% en lo que va de la semana, su peor registro para ese lapso desde junio. * Los futuros del oro estadounidense con entrega en diciembre cayeron un 1,1% a 4.014,60 dólares por onza. * El crudo Brent alcanzaba su máximo en más de cinco meses, después de que los ataques hutíes en Arabia Saudita avivaron la preocupación por nuevas interrupciones en el suministro energético. * "El aumento de las preocupaciones por la inflación sugiere que los principales bancos centrales del mundo no podrán flexibilizar sus políticas monetarias tan rápidamente como desearían. Todo ello juega en contra de los alcistas del mercado del oro y la plata en estos momentos", afirmó Jim Wyckoff, analista de mercado de American Gold Exchange. * La ola de ventas de acciones tecnológicas también ha provocado ajustes de márgenes para los operadores e inversores en renta variable, lo que les ha llevado a vender activos en oro y plata, añadió Wyckoff. * Los operadores esperan en su mayoría que la Fed mantenga las tasas de interés sin cambios en su reunión del 27 al 28 de octubre, aunque los datos de inflación al consumidor y al productor de Estados Unidos, publicados la semana pasada y mejores de lo esperado, reforzaron los argumentos a favor de una política monetaria más restrictiva a finales de este año. * Según la herramienta FedWatch de CME, ven un 92% de posibilidades de que la Fed mantenga las tasas la próxima semana y un 83% de probabilidad de una subida en diciembre. * Entre otros metales preciosos, la plata al contado cayó un 0,7% a 54,17 dólares por onza y el paladio bajó un 0,5% a 1.053,11 dólares, alcanzando mínimos desde noviembre de 2025 y junio de 2025, respectivamente. El platino al contado cayó un 0,5% a 1.562,11 dólares por onza, su nivel más bajo desde julio. Los tres metales anotaron caídas semanales.

item.title: London stocks mark weekly fall as oil hits five-month high ahead of budget
item.description: Britain's FTSE 100 snapped a two-week winning streak on Friday, as oil prices at over five-month highs weighed on risk appetite, ahead of finance minister John Healey's first budget next week.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Britain's FTSE 100 snapped a two-week winning streak on Friday, as oil prices at over five-month highs weighed on risk appetite, ahead of finance minister John Healey's first budget next week. The blue-chip FTSE 100 index (.FTSE) closed 0.3% lower at 10,690.36 points. The midcap FTSE 250 (.FTMC) ended 0.1% higher, but marked its sharpest weekly fall in six weeks. Energy shares (.FTNMX601010) advanced 3.9% as Brent crude crossed $115 a barrel Most sectors were lower, with aerospace and defence shares (.FTNMX502010) slipping 4.6% to an over five-month low Rolls-Royce (RR.L) slid 7.6%, registering its biggest one-day fall since April 2025. item.title: Nasdaq ticks up as tech stocks steady; SpaceX worries hit telecoms
item.description: The tech-heavy Nasdaq edged higher on Friday, helped by signs of stabilization in some tech stocks, while telecom shares tumbled on concerns that SpaceX's entry in the sector could heighten competition and threaten their market share.
item.dc:creator: Tharuniyaa Lakshmi, Ragini Mathur
item.content:encoded: The tech-heavy Nasdaq edged higher on Friday, helped by signs of stabilization in some tech stocks, while telecom shares tumbled on concerns that SpaceX's entry in the sector could heighten competition and threaten their market share. For the week, the benchmark S&P 500 and the Nasdaq were on track for losses, while the blue-chip Dow remained slightly higher, supported by gains in defensive stocks. The Philadelphia Semiconductor index (.SOX) rose 1.4%, as some chip-related stocks gained on Friday. Nvidia (NVDA.O) was up 0.3%, while Micron Technology (MU.O) and Intel (INTC.O) gained 2.5% and 3.8%, respectively. AI-related shares swung sharply this month, first coming under pressure over CoreWeave's (CRWV.O) [USN:L4N4620ZT TEXT:"debt burden"] and the cost of financing AI investment. On Thursday, the Nasdaq (.IXIC) fell again, logging the biggest single-day drop in four months. The slide accelerated following Meta's (META.O) nearly 8% [USN:L6N468125 TEXT:"decline"] after the company reported its first cash outflow in more than a decade amid concerns over its AI-related expenditures. CoreWeave shares were down 2.3% on Friday. "Investors are still trying to wrap their heads around the sheer size of this AI spend. The sheer size of these notional dollars is staggering, but we aren't at the point of the cycle yet that we've seen this return," said James O'Day, head of equities at Citizens Bank. "The market's probably healthier than it feels." The S&P 500 communication services index (.SPLRCL) was down 0.6%, as AT&T (T.N) , Verizon (VZ.N) and T-Mobile (TMUS.O) fell between 1.3% and 5.6% after a [USN:L4N4682CX TEXT:"report said"] SpaceX (SPCX.O) was in talks with cellular infrastructure companies about launching a nationwide wireless carrier program. SpaceX shares gained 2.2%. US cell tower operators gained from this news, with Crown Castle (CCI.N) up 11.11% and American Tower (AMT.N) up 4.8%. Market focus remains on the earnings season, with major companies such as Microsoft (MSFT.O) , Alphabet (GOOGL.O) and Amazon (AMZN.O) reporting next week. At 12:02 p.m. ET, the Dow Jones Industrial Average (.DJI) fell 502.87 points, or 0.95%, to 52,365.11, the S&P 500 (.SPX) lost 8.60 points, or 0.11%, to 7,654.90, and the Nasdaq Composite (.IXIC) gained 80.59 points, or 0.32%, to 26,091.45. Eight of 11 sectors on the S&P 500 declined, while the energy index (.SPNY) rose to a record high, tracking gains in oil prices, and the information technology sector rose 0.9%. Brent crude held near a more-than-five-month high amid Middle East supply concerns, adding to inflation worries ahead of the Federal Reserve's policy meeting next week. Markets expect the Fed to keep interest rates unchanged at its meeting next week, according to the CME's FedWatch Tool. Data from the University of Michigan showed [USN:L1N4690PT TEXT:"US consumer sentiment edged down"] near a record low in October, as rising prices because of the Middle East conflict soured households' views of the economy. S&P 500's third-quarter profit growth is now forecast at 32.3%, up from 30.7% previously, according to LSEG data. Among major movers, Comfort Systems (FIX.N) was the biggest loser on the benchmark index, with a 7.5% fall, despite its third-quarter revenue and profit beating estimates. Bloom Energy (BE.N) dropped 11.4% even after the [USN:L1N46819F TEXT:"energy firm raised"] its fiscal 2026 forecast. SLB (SLB.N) rose 7% after the oilfield services provider [USN:L4N4690VN TEXT:"beat Wall Street estimates"] for third-quarter profit. Declining issues outnumbered advancers by a 1.85-to-1 ratio on the NYSE and by a 1.54-to-1 ratio on the Nasdaq. The S&P 500 posted 17 new 52-week highs and 6 new lows, while the Nasdaq Composite recorded 54 new highs and 276 new lows.

item.title: El cobre repunta a medida que se estabilizan las existencias y los mercados bursátiles
item.description: Los precios del cobre repuntaron el viernes tras una fuerte caída en la sesión anterior, gracias a la estabilización de los mercados bursátiles y a la ralentización del aumento de las existencias.

semanas en la sesión anterior. * Los mercados de metales se vieron respaldados al remitir la caída de las acciones tecnológicas a nivel mundial, después de que las preocupaciones sobre las enormes necesidades de financiación de la inteligencia artificial sacudieron a Wall Street. * "Hoy hemos visto cómo los futuros del Nasdaq se recuperaban tras la venta masiva de ayer y esa es probablemente la razón por la que algunos inversores en metales están volviendo al mercado", dijo Ole Hansen, responsable de estrategia de materias primas de Saxo Bank en Copenhague. * Los inversores seguían mostrándose nerviosos y existía el riesgo de nuevas caídas en el cobre, especialmente si los precios rompen a la baja el mínimo de septiembre de 13.925 dólares, añadió. * Las preocupaciones por el exceso de existencias se disiparon después de que los datos diarios del viernes mostraron que las existencias de cobre de la LME aumentaron en 800 toneladas métricas, tras haber subido una quinta parte durante la semana pasada hasta alcanzar las 273.750 toneladas. * En China, las existencias en los almacenes registrados en la Bolsa de Futuros de Shanghái se desplomaron un 26,5%, mostraron datos semanales el viernes. * Los inversores seguían preocupados por el exceso de existencias en Estados Unidos, que ha atraído enormes flujos de cobre debido a la especulación sobre la imposición de aranceles por parte del Gobierno, señaló Hansen. * El níquel fue el que peor comportamiento registró en la LME, cediendo un 1,6% a 15.865 dólares por tonelada, mientras los operadores esperaban señales más claras de las empresas chinas que barajan recortes coordinados de la producción en sus operaciones en Indonesia. * El Grupo Internacional de Estudio del Níquel pronosticó la semana pasada un pequeño excedente mundial para este año, revirtiendo así una previsión anterior de déficit. * Entre otros metales básicos en la LME, el aluminio subió un 1,2% a 3.044 dólares por tonelada, el zinc ganó un 2,2% a 3.752 dólares, el plomo sumó un 0,6% a 1.909 dólares y el estaño avanzó un 1,2% a 50.700 dólares.

item.title: Brent se dispara a nivel más alto desde abril por ataques hutíes en A.Saudita y vertido de petróleo
item.description: Los precios del petróleo subieron el viernes y el Brent llegó a su nivel más alto desde finales de abril después de que los ataques de los hutíes en Arabia Saudita avivaran la preocupación por nuevas interrupciones en el suministro energético procedente de Oriente Medio, donde las autoridades de los Emiratos Árabes Unidos también informaron de un vertido de petróleo.
item.dc:creator: Nicole Jao
item.content:encoded: Los precios del petróleo subieron el viernes y el Brent llegó a su nivel más alto desde finales de abril después de que los ataques de los hutíes en Arabia Saudita avivaran la preocupación por nuevas interrupciones en el suministro energético procedente de Oriente Medio, donde las autoridades de los Emiratos Árabes Unidos también informaron de un vertido de petróleo. * Los futuros del crudo Brent subían 4,01 dólares, un 3,54%, a 117,18 dólares el barril a las 1622 GMT. El máximo de la sesión, de 117,38 dólares, fue un pico desde finales de abril. El crudo West Texas Intermediate (WTI) de Estados Unidos subió 3,75 dólares, o un 3,77%, a 103,22 dólares. * El índice de referencia del Brent apunta a registrar un alza semanal del 6,7%, lo que supondría su tercera semana consecutiva de ganancias. El WTI camina a cerrar la semana con un alza del 1,8%. * Saudi Aramco (2222.SE) ordenó el jueves la evacuación de su sede central en Dhahran, en el Golfo, cerca de Baréin, según informó Reuters. Se intensificaron los combates entre el mayor exportador de crudo del mundo y los hutíes, con base en Yemen. * Por otra parte, se detectó un vertido de petróleo procedente de un petrolero frente a la costa de Umm Al Quwain, en los Emiratos Árabes Unidos, dijo el viernes el ministerio de Cambio Climático y Medio Ambiente de los EAU. No se especificó la causa del vertido y las autoridades aún no han identificado el petrolero implicado. * Fuentes del sector naviero afirmaron el 9 de octubre que el Gem No. 2 fue alcanzado por un proyectil no identificado a 13 millas náuticas al oeste de Al Jazeera, en los EAU. * "El mercado está preocupado por estos continuos ataques iraníes contra petroleros, que han aumentado durante la última semana", afirmó Andrew Lipow, presidente de Lipow Oil Associates. "Aunque se ha producido un aumento del tránsito de petróleo a través del estrecho de Ormuz, la situación podría cambiar en cualquier momento". * Los enfrentamientos entre los hutíes y la coalición liderada por Arabia Saudita, que respalda al Gobierno de Yemen reconocido internacionalmente, se han recrudecido desde que los hutíes, alineados con Irán, avanzaron el mes pasado hacia Bab el-Mandeb, un punto estratégico para el transporte marítimo situado en la desembocadura del mar Rojo. * Octubre ha sido el peor mes en cuanto a ataques contra el transporte marítimo comercial en el estrecho de Ormuz y las vías navegables cercanas, según datos recopilados por un centro de estudios con sede en Washington que lleva desde 2017 realizando un seguimiento de los incidentes de seguridad marítima en todo el mundo. * El presidente Donald Trump afirmó el viernes que Estados Unidos podría poner fin rápidamente a la guerra con Irán, pero señaló que quizá Washington debería permitir que el conflicto se fuera apagando gradualmente.

item.title: Trump's diesel price relief efforts grow costlier as election nears
item.description: With the November midterm elections fast approaching, President Donald Trump is throwing an array of costly and politically fraught solutions at one stubborn problem: the price of diesel.
item.dc:creator: Jarrett Renshaw, Leah Douglas
item.content:encoded: With the November midterm elections fast approaching, President Donald Trump is throwing an array of costly and politically fraught solutions at one stubborn problem: the price of diesel. His administration has offered billions of dollars to farmers, relaxed rules for truckers, [USN:S0N43U024 TEXT:"eased sanctions"] on Russian fuel and pressured European allies to release emergency stocks. Yet diesel prices rose again last week, leaving Trump spending political and financial capital without delivering the relief his party wants as voters go to the polls. Republicans are defending narrow majorities in Congress, and high costs are a major concern for voters. Nearly 80% of Americans [USN:L6N45T0W3 TEXT:"blame"] Trump for higher costs, according to an October Reuters/Ipsos poll. US diesel prices [USN:L6N45Z19G TEXT:"rose nearly 10 cents a gallon"] in the latest week to an average of $6.28, reversing two weeks of declines and remaining near record highs, according to the Energy Information Administration. Diesel in the last two months has become a central issue not only in the midterms but as a catalyst driving up already-elevated US inflation. The fuel is critical for farmers, construction companies, freight operators and more, and government data last week showed its rise was partly behind hefty increases in delivery costs, early-stage food production costs and [USN:L6N461198 TEXT:"even toy prices"]. The political pressure is particularly acute in traditionally Republican Farm Belt states like [USN:L6N44F10S TEXT:"Iowa"] and [USN:L6N45F193 TEXT:"Kansas"], where rising fuel and fertilizer costs, trade disruptions and weak farm economics have fueled discontent among some of Trump's core supporters. Trump has promoted his diesel measures at campaign [USN:L1N45Q06H TEXT:"rallies"] across the region. He signed an executive order onstage in Nebraska allowing red-dyed diesel to be used in highway vehicles and announced $8 billion in new farm aid during a rally in Kansas on Monday. The measures illustrate the trade-offs Trump is accepting in pursuit of near-term relief. The new aid adds fresh strain on federal spending, while the Russian fuel move risks helping Moscow finance its war in Ukraine. Pressure on European allies to release emergency stocks, backed by a threat to restrict US diesel exports, has created diplomatic friction. “The president tends to discount long-term losses over short-term gain, and I am skeptical if there is any short gain to be had here,” said Chris Borick, a pollster and political scientist at Muhlenberg College in Pennsylvania. The White House attributed high diesel prices to “pre-existing issues,” including years of refinery closures and damage from Russia's war in Ukraine, while defending Trump's efforts to ease costs. “The President wants diesel prices to fall, which is why he has taken historic actions to save American farmers, truckers, and workers every hard-earned penny," White House spokeswoman Taylor Rogers said. SKEPTICISM AND UNANSWERED QUESTIONS One of Trump's most direct attempts to lower diesel costs has struggled to gain traction. Trump signed an executive order this month [USN:L1N461138 TEXT:"allowing truckers to use red-dyed diesel"], typically intended for off-road use such as farm equipment, for highway driving while temporarily avoiding certain federal tax reporting and record-keeping requirements. But the IRS has not eliminated the federal diesel tax, instead temporarily waiving related reporting requirements and penalties through year-end, leaving uncertainty for truck stops and fuel sellers. David Fialkov, top lobbyist at NATSO, a trade group representing the largest US truck stop operators, said members appreciate Trump's effort to tackle diesel costs but that the guidance remains "murky" and carries too much risk. "I really don’t see any of these dyed diesel announcements making a meaningful dent in diesel prices," Fialkov said. Trump is also turning to federal payments to cushion some of the constituencies feeling the pain. Government payments to farmers were already expected to top $47 billion this year, buoyed by commodity payments and $12 billion in tariff relief [USN:S0N3VI02L TEXT:"distributed "]by the US Department of Agriculture earlier this year. The $8 billion farm relief program would push the total to a record $55.4 billion, exceeding the previous high of $45 billion in 2020, when farmers received pandemic assistance. The payments can help farmers manage higher costs and lost sales but do not directly address the market disruptions driving up fuel and fertilizer prices. They also raise questions about taxpayer spending to compensate producers for damage that farm groups say is linked partly to the administration’s own trade and foreign policies. “This is the second round of emergency aid this year to address losses that were largely foreseeable,” National Farmers Union President Rob Larew said. “Trade disruptions and rising fuel costs tied to conflict abroad have put family farmers in a difficult position, and one-time payments can't provide the stability they need to plan for the future.” The aid will arrive after the November 3 election, and likely not reach farmers until the end of the year, USDA official Richard Fordyce [USN:L6N4690W3 TEXT:"told Reuters"] on Friday. FRICTION OVER RUSSIAN FUEL Some of Trump's efforts to increase diesel supplies carry geopolitical trade-offs. His decision to ease sanctions on Russian diesel that were designed to restrict Moscow’s energy revenues and limit its ability to finance its war in Ukraine has [USN:L1N45Z0TJ TEXT:"drawn bipartisan criticism"] -- and raised questions about whether the move will meaningfully lower US fuel prices. Trump has defended the sanctions relief as necessary to draw Russian President Vladimir Putin into negotiations to end the war in Ukraine and to release American prisoner Stephen Hubbard. As the administration's intervention efforts have failed to lower fuel costs, Trump has sought to shift blame toward Ukraine and President Volodymyr Zelenskiy rather than the Iran war ahead of the elections. Analysts say the Iran conflict has been the much bigger driver of the diesel price spike, disrupting global oil flows and refined-fuel supplies, while Ukrainian attacks on Russian refineries have helped tighten supplies but played a more limited role in the price. “I sort of see it as a blame-shifting kind of scapegoating operation, more than a genuine attempt to moderate prices in the lead-up to the election,” said Edward Fishman, director of the Maurice R. Greenberg Center at the Council on Foreign Relations.

item.title: Saudi missile plant expansion may produce more powerful missiles, study says
item.description: Saudi Arabia appears to be expanding its ballistic missile factory to build larger solid-fuel missiles that could fly farther or carry heavier payloads, according to two US researchers who analyzed more than a year of commercial satellite images.
item.dc:creator: Jonathan Landay
item.content:encoded: Saudi Arabia appears to be expanding its ballistic missile factory to build larger solid-fuel missiles that could fly farther or carry heavier payloads, according to two US researchers who analyzed more than a year of commercial satellite images. More capable missiles could help Saudi Arabia to deter attacks by Iran and make its military more self-reliant, while possibly strengthening its position in a deadly conflict with Yemen's Tehran-backed Houthi fighters. But they risk fueling a regional missile race and could deepen opposition in the US Congress to a US-Saudi civilian nuclear agreement that has already raised concerns about proliferation. Satellite company Planet Labs, based in the US, took images of the al-Duwadimi complex about 125 miles (200 km) west of Riyadh between April 2025 and September 2026. A satellite image shows the solid propellant motor plant in Al Duwadimi, Saudi Arabia, May 6, 2025. Planet Labs PBC/Handout via REUTERS A satellite image shows the solid propellant motor plant in Al Duwadimi, Saudi Arabia, September 18, 2026. Planet Labs PBC/Handout via REUTERS The two researchers, Sam Lair and Michael Duitsman of the Foreign Policy Research Institute, assessed that those images show a new building that houses casting pits — wells in which a mixture of fuel ingredients is poured into missile motor casings and allowed to harden. The Saudi embassy and Information Ministry did not respond to requests for comment. The building, flanked by what appear to be walls to protect nearby structures from accidental explosions, is at least twice as large as the one believed to house the plant’s existing casting pits, Lair and Duitsman said in their assessment. The Foreign Policy Research Institute (FPRI) is a non-partisan research organization in Philadelphia. A second new building could be used to store fuel ingredients or finished missile components, they said. The imagery "suggests that Saudi Arabia is expanding the infrastructure at the missile production complex, likely to produce larger missiles which could deliver larger payloads or reach longer ranges," they wrote. Militaries favor solid-fuel missiles because they can be stored for long periods and launched more quickly than liquid-fuel systems. Lair and Duitsman and experts from the London-based International Institute for Strategic Studies (IISS) and the CNA research and analysis organization told Reuters that the makeup of Saudi Arabia's missile force suggests that the al-Duwadimi complex relies on Chinese technology. Lair and Duitsman said that its characteristics also are similar to Chinese missile plants. Saudi Arabia secretly acquired about 40 liquid-fuel DF-3 ballistic missiles from China in 1987, according to a 1991 declassified CIA estimate. It displayed two of them for the first time in an April 2014 military parade, according to a Youtube video and photographs of the event. The FPRI team also recently identified from social media videos and photos what they assessed was the wreckage in Yemen of a Saudi-fired Chinese-designed DF-15 missile. Lair said the kingdom may now be producing the solid-fuel DF-15, and that the expansion of a1-Dumadimi is likely for the production of the longer-range DF-21 or a similar missile. Riyadh is believed to have turned to Beijing because Washington has long restricted exports of longer-range missile systems. The Chinese embassy and defense ministry did not respond to requests for comment. The CIA declined to comment. The White House did not respond to a request for comment. MISSILES WOULD ALTER THE BALANCE OF POWER Sascha Bruchmann, a research fellow at IISS, said longer-range missiles would allow Saudi Arabia to strike Iran without risking its US-supplied F-15 jet fighters against Iranian air defenses. “You’d want a system to threaten whatever is holy to Tehran ... if you don’t have the political will to send an F-15 with JDAMs over Tehran,” said Bruchmann, referring to US-made satellite-guided bombs. “Iran has a lead because its missiles and drones can strike Saudi wherever it wants. The Saudis could close that capability gap a bit.” Bruchmann, who reviewed the FPRI analysis at Reuters request, concurred that the expansion of al-Duwadimi could be for producing more powerful solid-fuel missiles. Janes, the defense intelligence company, also reviewed it and said the buildings “may suggest an effort to expand production capability or support the development of longer-range missiles.” Saudi Arabia's apparent pursuit of more powerful missiles comes as other Gulf powers are also seeking to expand their offensive and defensive arsenals, said Decker Eveleth, a CNA analyst who has been tracking the al-Duwadimi construction with commercial satellite imagery and concurred with the FPRI assessment. “This is being replicated across the Middle East,” he said. “You see exactly the same thing happening in the UAE. You see the exact same thing happening in Turkey. Everybody is doing this now.” The expansion of al-Duwadimi could have political consequences in the US by stiffening bipartisan congressional opposition to a US-Saudi agreement under which the US would help Riyadh establish uranium enrichment for power generation. Opponents say that the deal lacks sufficient safeguards to prevent Riyadh from secretly building a nuclear weapon. The kingdom has denied any such plan. WORK BEGAN LAST YEAR The FPRI assessment said the Planet Labs imagery showed that the expansion at al-Duwadimi began in April 2025 with ground-clearing and digging for the suspected storage building. Work on the suspected casting-pit building began later that month or in early May, it said. A December 12, 2025, photo showed what researchers assessed were two deep pits inside the building that had no roof yet. A satellite image shows the solid propellant motor plant in Al Duwadimi, Saudi Arabia, December 12, 2025. Planet Labs PBC/Handout via REUTERS A September 18, 2026, photo shows the roof still partly missing and "heavy duty blast diverting walls" on either side to prevent accidental explosions from damaging adjacent structures. A satellite image shows the solid propellant motor plant in Al Duwadimi, Saudi Arabia, September 18, 2026. Planet Labs PBC/Handout via REUTERS The walls, the researchers said, are somewhat similar to those depicted in imagery of US and Iranian missile plants and "further evidence the building is for casting solid propellant motors." Finishing the roofs would not take long, the FPRI said, but installing casting equipment may take several months. The facility could be ready to start producing missiles as early as the end of the year.

item.title: Zymeworks licenses experimental lung cancer drug to Roche in up to $813 million deal
item.description: Zymeworks said on Friday Roche has gained rights to develop and commercialize its experimental lung cancer drug under a global licensing deal worth up to $813 million.
item.dc:creator: Sahil Pandey
item.content:encoded: Zymeworks (ZYME.O) said on Friday Roche (ROPC.S) has gained rights to develop and commercialize its experimental lung cancer drug under a global licensing deal worth up to $813 million. Zymeworks will receive $55 million upfront and an additional $40 million when the Swiss drugmaker begins a planned dose-optimization study of the drug ZW209 Roche will take over the development of the treatment after Zymeworks completes the dose-escalation portion of an ongoing early-stage study The company said the drug targets DLL3, a protein commonly found on small-cell lung cancer cells but rarely seen in healthy tissue Roche has agreed to partner on ZW209 before efficacy data were available because of "the innovation and differentiation in our trispecific T-cell engager platform," Zymeworks CEO Kenneth Galbraith told Reuters The first patient is expected to be enrolled before the end of 2026, Galbraith said The company said it could receive up to $718 million in development, regulatory and commercial milestone payments, in addition to tiered royalties on future sales

item.title: Dr Reddy's rolls out new generic Ozempic brands to ease Obeda supply hit
item.description: Dr Reddy's Laboratories has expanded its portfolio of generic versions of Ozempic with two new brands to fill a supply-chain hit to its original Obeda injections, product photographs and marketing materials reviewed by Reuters show.
item.dc:creator: Rishika Sadam
item.content:encoded: Dr Reddy's Laboratories (REDY.NS) has expanded its portfolio of generic versions of Ozempic with two new brands to fill a supply-chain hit to its original Obeda injections, product photographs and marketing materials reviewed by Reuters show. The shift, first reported here by Reuters, follows supply disruptions that hit sales of Dr Reddy's Obeda injection in India's fast-growing market for semaglutide, which is the active ingredient in Novo Nordisk's weight-loss drug Wegovy. Shares in Dr Reddy's fell by as much as 2% after the Reuters report, before paring some losses to settle 1.4% lower. Dr Reddy's [USN:L4N4060Y5 TEXT:"launched"] Obeda, a generic version of Novo Nordisk's (NOVOb.CO) diabetes drug, in India in March and later in Canada after semaglutide lost patent protection, setting off a race among domestic drugmakers to launch lower-cost versions. The drugmaker said at a media briefing on Friday that after encountering manufacturing issues with Obeda in July, it had shifted production to a partner's facility to maintain supplies. Dr Reddy's said that its Obeda Pro and Obeda Plus would remain available in the market and could be used for diabetes treatment and weight management. Obeda Pro and Obeda Plus are manufactured by a different firm than the Obeda injectable, supplies of which were halted after Dr Reddy's found an impurity in the active ingredient. Several distributors told Reuters that Dr Reddy's is likely to discontinue Obeda and will focus on Obeda Pro and Obeda Plus. "The company said there were some technical issues with Obeda injectable, and they recalled stocks from us. They said they would instead supply Obeda Pro," a drug distributor said. "When we started off on semaglutide, we basically had two sources for the product. One was our own product and one through the partner product," M.V. Ramana, chief executive of Global Generics, said on Friday. Having multiple semaglutide brands should not be interpreted as evidence of one replacing another, the company told Reuters earlier. A company notice reviewed by Reuters showed Dr Reddy's recalled Obeda injections in July "for technical evaluation". An oral version of the drug was not recalled. The company had also recalled batches of generic semaglutide in Canada in August because of the impurity issue. It will relaunch the drug in Canada this quarter and is targeting launches in Latin America and Africa in coming months. Research firm Pharmarack estimated in March that the domestic market for semaglutide drugs will grow to 80 billion rupees ($844 million) by 2030. Dr Reddy's said in July that supplies of Obeda injections would be [USN:L4N43B09O TEXT:"unavailable"] until November and analysts warned it risked losing market share if supplies were not restored soon. On Friday, Dr Reddy's said it was on track to resolve the impurity issue and relaunch next month. Packaging materials showed Obeda was manufactured by contract manufacturer OneSource Specialty Pharma (ONEO.NS) . Obeda Pro and Obeda Plus, which began appearing in the market in late July according to supply invoices reviewed by Reuters, are manufactured by Hetero Labs. Both are available in different dose strengths, just like Ozempic and Wegovy. Hetero Labs and OneSource Specialty Pharma did not respond to requests for comment. Dr Reddy's had sold about 442,000 units of generic semaglutide in India through September, research firm Pharmarack said. By comparison, India's largest drugmaker Sun Pharma (SUN.NS) sold 151,000 semaglutide units. ($1 = 94.7875 Indian rupees)

item.title: Weight-loss drugs fuel protein boom, but with more consumer scrutiny
item.description: Even as consumers seek out new sources of protein for their diets, they are becoming more skeptical of foods advertised as high-protein.
item.dc:creator: Waylon Cunningham, Nicholas Brown
item.content:encoded: Protein-infused bottled water. Ice cream. Boxed macaroni and cheese. Even vodka. The rise of weight-loss drugs is driving a boom in protein-based products, as users of GLP-1 medication like Novo Nordisk's (NOVOb.CO) Ozempic and Eli Lilly's (LLY.N) Mounjaro look for ways to counter the muscle loss those drugs can cause. GLP-1 users say they will spend 11% more on high-protein foods than before starting the drugs, according to an August survey from Boston Consulting Group. This is the fifth story in a five-part Reuters series on how weight-loss drugs are changing the way people shop and eat, and how companies are responding to the trend. Even as consumers seek out new sources of protein for their diets, they are becoming more skeptical of foods advertised as high-protein, Reuters interviews with consumers and company executives found. Some shoppers question whether products contain as much protein as advertising implies, while blanching at those that pack in so many additives or sugar that they undercut the health pitch. A report from marketing research firm NielsenIQ earlier this year said the snack industry has entered its "accountability era," noting that 25% of its survey respondents this year said they are using scanning apps to check the nutritional value of products, up from around 17% last year. "Protein is no longer a differentiator," said Chris Costagli, a lead marketing researcher at NielsenIQ, who co-wrote the report. Megan Gisela Bautista, a nonprofit employee in Maryland who does strength training, was recently disappointed by the protein content of a chicken jerky snack that touted high protein in a large, colorful font. "I'd have to eat five of them," Bautista said. "That's bad for you." Zack Spears of Dallas said he is checking nutritional labels regularly, and now watches YouTube videos from an online content creator who reviews protein-marketed products. "As this protein craze pops off, and things are getting more expensive, I want to be sure what I'm putting in my body is healthy," Spears said. Some brands acknowledge the growing consumer scrutiny. “Protein is here to stay, but the conversation must evolve,” said Susan Zaripheh, North America chief research officer for yogurt maker Danone (DANO.PA) , in a statement to Reuters. “Consumers are starting to look ‘beyond the gram,’ becoming more informed in the nuances of protein source and nutrient density.” Over the summer, the French food company filed a false advertising [USN:L6N42P17H TEXT:"lawsuit"] against rival yogurt maker Chobani, accusing it of inflating its protein claims on labels by using non-standard serving sizes. Chobani has disputed those claims, telling Reuters in a statement that its labeling is accurate and transparent. Zaripheh said consumers want products that also aid in digestibility and contain other nutrients like fiber. In addition to existing high-protein yogurts and soy milks, the company is developing products that combine protein with other nutrients. Globe Market Research estimated over the summer that the worldwide protein-enriched food market was worth nearly $58 billion last year. But Hormel Foods (HRL.N) , well-known for protein-heavy products like Spam and canned lunch meats, said it is avoiding the use of additives to increase protein in its products. "We believe that in the long run, people don't want too much science in their food," said Jason Levine, Hormel chief marketing officer, referring to additives like "whey powder or pea powder or scientifically engineered protein isolates." SCRUTINIZING LABELS Reuters found several brands that advertise protein content based on a larger portion size than used in regular versions of the same product, including in pastas, oatmeals and granolas. Nature Valley, a snack brand owned by General Mills (GIS.N) , sells a version of its “oats ‘n honey” loose granola that advertises 13 grams of protein on its packaging, based on a 2/3 cup (65 grams) serving size, more than twice as big as the 1/4 cup (27 grams) it calls a serving size for its regular, non-enhanced granola. General Mills, in a statement, said it considers the regular version a snack while the protein version can be eaten either as a snack or a more complete cereal meal. The product's protein-to-calorie ratio, a metric dietitians use to describe a product's protein content, indicates a “very low amount of protein overall,” said Jonathan Bonnet, a Stanford professor and chief medical officer at the Ardmore Institute of Health, adding that a glass of skim milk has more protein than the 2/3-cup serving. Bonnet said more patients are asking him lately for guidance on their protein intake. Still, other companies are expanding their offerings to meet demand. Researcher Circana reported in August that around 48% of US adults are looking to add protein in their diets, up 7 points from last year. Discount supermarket chain Aldi recently told Reuters it is launching a new line of private-label protein pancakes in October, the latest in a string of high-protein items released this year that have included sparkling water, crackers and wagyu beef jerky. Walmart will start selling a new, protein-infused instant coffee product from J.M. Smucker's (SJM.N) Folgers from November until January exclusively, Walmart told Reuters last month. Some consumers and dietitians say the protein trend has led people to eat more protein than they need. NielsenIQ's report said a third of more than 1,000 surveyed respondents believe the food industry is overhyping protein — and another third believe some products have too much protein. Dana Hunnes, a professor and clinical dietitian at UCLA, says the average person doesn't need as much protein as industry marketing has promoted. And some protein-marketed products have too many processed ingredients to qualify as healthy, Hunnes said. “I’ve seen the equivalent of a candy bar” advertising protein, she said. “Just because it has protein doesn’t mean it’s something you should eat."
